544851|2026-06.headline: MV Electrosystems expects propulsion output to ramp from 10 units in September to about 40 per month by January, against an order book of 564 propulsion systems worth about INR989 crores.
544851|2026-06.overview: This was the first investor call after the company's listing, with no reported financials in the transcript. Management said deliveries have been limited to 2 or 3 small batches so far, with none in the prior two months, and that IPO proceeds (working capital) now fund a scale-up. Management targets about INR400 crore of revenue this year and roughly 10% PAT once run-rate is reached, though it conceded margins are negative or constrained during the initial ramp. Growth optionality was discussed across EMU/MEMU/Vande Bharat distributed propulsion, OHE auto fault locators (with PNC Technologies), and marine/electrical adjacencies.

financial_highlights.metric: Supply price per locomotive propulsion system
financial_highlights.value: INR1.67 crore (AMC roughly matches this figure over 3 years)

financial_highlights.metric: Working capital requirement at ~INR1,000 crore turnover

financial_highlights.value: 105 days stated in prospectus; last three cycles completed in 85 days

segments.name: Locomotive propulsion systems
segments.commentary: Order book of 564 units valued at about INR989 crore; ramp planned at 10 units in September, 25 in November, 40 per month by January. Capacity built for 55 per month, with 40 chosen as the stable target.

segments.name: EMU/MEMU/Vande Bharat distributed propulsion
segments.commentary: INR86 crore MCF EMU development order with 24-month supply window; design and development targeted in 8-10 months, then approval taking about 15-16 months in total. A 12-coach EMU is about INR16 crore and a 16-coach Vande Bharat about INR40 crore including electrics.

segments.name: Overhead electrification (OHE) / AFL
segments.commentary: Auto fault locator tied up with PNC Technologies (South Korea). Management pegged unit prices at INR12 lakh (sectioning/sub-sectioning) to INR36 lakh (substation transformer), roughly INR1 crore of revenue per transformer section, with installations expected over 5-7 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR400 crore, described as achievable definitively.
Monthly run-rate of about 40 propulsion systems from January, implying roughly INR70 crore a month and about 480 units a year.
PAT of 10%-plus expected once run-rate is reached; management expects profitability within 2-3 months and margins to improve month over month after stabilisation.
R&D spend to be 3%-4% of revenue over time; R&D team to be expanded with a new centre ready by Q3.
Approximately 15-16 months to EMU propulsion approval including development.
capex_capacity: Capacity built for 55 locomotive propulsion systems per month; company plans to run at 40 for consistency, with spare capacity earmarked for EMU propulsion.
Unit 2 already set up; box fabrication and assembly to start the following Monday after the call.
No further machinery capex planned; only test setups are required, with three more ordered and installations expected in 45-60 days.
Two additional shifts planned in the existing factory, cited as enabling about 4,500 systems.
demand_pricing: Management cited Indian Railways building about 1,600-1,700 locomotives a year, about 15,000 locomotives in service needing rehabilitation, and 300-500 EMUs tendered or to be tendered this year.

Locomotive tenders in pipeline: CLW tender for about 748 locomotives (expected around 31 August), followed by BLW and PLW tenders, expected over the next few weeks; more than 100 EMU propulsion tenders and 200 train-set electrical tenders published by ICF Chennai, not yet bid.

Company said it won about 25-26% of tendered locomotive propulsion quantity, with competitors including Siemens, Alstom, ABB, Medha and BHEL. In the last tender, 7 suppliers were awarded small quantities.
Management said margins were very thin across bidders; company was L2 in two tenders and L1 in one. Bulk purchasing (200-300 sets) was cited as offsetting electronics price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will the PLW/CLW propulsion tender cancellation affect the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was unaware of any cancellation and noted an active CLW tender for 748 locomotives. Tender-to-order conversion typically takes 45 days, sometimes up to 90.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company meet the December 26 order deadline, and what is the run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply obligations extend to March and into next financial year. Output is planned at 10 units in September, 25 in November, and 40 in January; extensions are typically granted for capacity-constrained suppliers.

qa_highlights.question: What margins apply given rising electronics costs and no price-escalation clause?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 10%-plus PAT at full run-rate; early months will have constrained or negative margins. Bulk procurement of 200-300 sets is offsetting global price increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle and requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement lead times range from 7 days to 6 months, averaging about 45 days. Payments were received within 15 days on all three dispatches. Working capital of about INR200 crore needed for roughly INR1,000 crore turnover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the realisation per propulsion system?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply price is INR1.67 crore per locomotive propulsion system; AMC over three years roughly matches that figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EMU/MCF approval process and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Three-month validation at the MCF commissioning depot, performance trials on Delhi-Ambala Road, then a four-month trial covering about 30,000 km before approval.

risks_watch: Execution risk on the ramp from 10 units in September to 40 per month by January, with management admitting near-term margins are negative or constrained.
Gross margin pressure from electronics price inflation with no price-escalation clause, and bids were won at thin margins (L1/L2).
Working capital intensity: about INR200 crore required; management quoted a 105-day cycle in the prospectus and 85 days on the last three cycles, with inconsistent figures raised by analysts.
Competitive intensity from Siemens, Alstom, ABB, Medha, BHEL and new entrants; the company holds about 25-26% share of tendered quantity.
EMU/Vande Bharat revenue depends on approval about 15-16 months out and an MCF delivery window of 24 months.
Unverified tender cancellation reported by an analyst on GeM (CLW, 127 sets); management disputed knowledge of it.
544851|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term opportunity, with specific numbers on ramp and margins. Evasive or vague on several points, including tender cancellation, the 238-day working capital figure, and the timing of the first-year PAT. Several answers were long and repetitive.
key_quotes: We see about 10% plus PAT margin comfortably coming in from this order.
Completely in-house. It'll be designed and developed completely with our own IPR, with our own technology in-house.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management targets 10%-plus PAT once the run-rate reaches 40 units/month, with margins improving month over month after stabilisation, though early months are negative or constrained and electronics costs are rising without an escalation clause.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Unit 2 is already commissioned for 55 propulsion systems/month, but management plans to run at 40/month, and two extra shifts (about 4,500 systems) are planned for Q2 FY27 with a new R&D centre ready by Q3.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Output is planned at 10 units in September, 25 in November and 40 in January, against a 564-unit order book (about 480 units a year at 40/month), with the company already winning about 25-26% of tendered quantity.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No further machinery capex is planned; only three test setups (45-60 days to install) are ordered, and capacity for 55/month already exists versus a 40/month target.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is guiding INR400 crore FY27 revenue as a firm target with no sign of beating it, and deliveries so far are only 2-3 small batches with none in the prior two months.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The ramp runs from 10 units in September to 40/month by January with management admitting near-term margins are negative or constrained, and the 105-day vs 85-day working capital cycle figures were inconsistent.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: EMU propulsion approval takes about 15-16 months including development (design in 8-10 months), and the INR86 crore MCF EMU order has a 24-month supply window, so new-product revenue comes later than the window.

rows.label: Locomotive propulsion order book conversion
rows.why: A 564-unit order book worth about INR989 crore is tentative, and tender-to-order conversion takes about 45 days (up to 90), with CLW tender for 748 locomotives expected around 31 August and BLW/PLW tenders to follow.

rows.label: EMU/Vande Bharat propulsion tenders
rows.why: More than 100 EMU propulsion tenders and 200 train-set electrical tenders from ICF Chennai are published but not yet bid, and the INR86 crore MCF order needs about 15-16 months to approval.

rows.label: Working capital build for ramp
rows.why: About INR200 crore of working capital is needed for roughly INR1,000 crore turnover, with procurement lead times averaging about 45 days (7 days to 6 months), and the IPO proceeds fund the scale-up.

tone.note: Management was confident on the INR400 crore FY27 revenue target, the 40/month run-rate and 10%-plus PAT, but was vague on the tender cancellation, the 105-day vs 85-day working capital cycle and first-year PAT timing; analysts pushed on those points.

544853|2026-06.headline: Juniper Green Q1 FY27 revenue rose 79% YoY to INR 324 crore and EBITDA 86% to INR 294 crore, with 601 MWp commissioned in the quarter.
544853|2026-06.overview: First results call as a listed company: total income INR 324 crore (+79% YoY), EBITDA INR 294 crore (+86%) at a 91% margin, and PAT INR 33 crore (+54%). Fleet CUF rose to 30.2% from 28.2% and generation grew 72% to 944 million units. Management reported record commissioning of 601 MWp in the quarter and won new SECI FDRE/thermal-mimic and GUVNL wind tenders after quarter end. Net debt-to-equity was 3.24x before IPO proceeds of INR 1,800 crore; net worth is now stated at INR 5,200 crore.

segments.name: Solar + wind operations
segments.commentary: Fleet CUF 30.2% (vs 28.2%); generation 944 million units. Wind portfolio of 190 MW delivered 49.9% weighted average CUF, plant availability 98.8%, grid availability 99.6%.

segments.name: Commissioning
segments.commentary: 601 MWp commissioned in Q1 (458 MWp solar, 143 MW wind), the highest quarterly addition, plus ~400 MWh BESS. Over 760 MW and ~400 MWh BESS commissioned April to date across 8 sites.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: Target ~4.5 GWh installed by June 2027 and ~10 GWh by March 2028; ~4 GWh additional orders placed with Envision. Round-trip efficiency ~91%, state of health ~99.6%.

segments.name: Portfolio
segments.commentary: Total portfolio ~11,200 MW plus ~9 GWh BESS; operational plus PPA-signed capacity above 6.2 GW. FDRE and wind-solar hybrid are 84% of the portfolio at blended weighted average tariff of INR 3.7/unit.

guidance_outlook: FY27: ~2 GW of renewable capacity additions targeted; 250-300 MW planned in Q2 FY27; ~4 GW total capacity by FY27 with run-rate EBITDA ~INR 2,750 crore for the 2 GW added.
FY28: ~6 GW to be commissioned with run-rate EBITDA ~INR 4,500 crore.
Current 2,575 MW commissioned has run-rate EBITDA of INR 1,620 crore; March 2026 capacity contributes INR 1,050 crore.
Capex ~INR 16,000 crore as of 30 June 2026, expected to rise to ~INR 22,000 crore by March 2027 (including ~3,900 MW commissioning by then).
Transmission: remaining ~1 GW substations largely operational; one ~300 MW substation expected to complete by December 2026.
Bikaner 50 MW merchant plant curtailment ~2-2.5%; 100 MWh battery doubling to 200 MWh expected within a month.
capex_capacity: 601 MWp commissioned in Q1 FY27 (458 MWp solar, 143 MW wind), the highest quarterly commissioning; ~400 MWh BESS also commissioned.
Surplus connectivity above 4.5 GW over the full pipeline; connectivity for more than 20 GWh of further BESS; over 14,000 acres of land banked and 200+ identified wind locations.
Module procurement closed at INR 12.1-12.2/Wp non-DCR; DCR modules assumed at ~INR 17/Wp for the thermal-mimic tender.
BESS sourced fully integrated from Envision (containers with AESC cells, PCS, EMS via Universe); container prices ~USD 58-60/kWh for early batches, ~USD 65-68 for later, all-in ~USD 100-110/kWh.
Thermal-mimic tender (SECI, 870 MW / 2,200 MWh, Rajasthan) has grid connectivity available; COD timing to follow PPA signing.
demand_pricing: Two tenders won after quarter end: SECI FDRE/thermal-mimic (870 MW, 2,200 MWh BESS against 230 MW contracted, tariff INR 5.26/unit; letter of award received) and a 50 MW GUVNL wind project at INR 3.51/unit.
Signed a 50 MW PPA with SJVN under FDRE at INR 4.25/unit; 550 MW FDRE capacity remains unsigned, with 350 MW in advanced discussions and a further 150 MW hybrid in very advanced discussions.
98% of contracted capacity is with off-takers rated A and above; 98% of portfolio under long-term PPAs, typically 25 years.
Merchant BESS: ~1.5 GWh of capacity not yet linked to projects will run merchant; some power sold on HPDAM at up to INR 20/unit; charging cost ~INR 1-1.50/unit.
Standalone BESS not pursued as returns are low; new tenders target higher-teens returns on an overall basis.

financial_highlights.change: +54% YoY; includes ~INR 18 crore one-time refinancing cost

financial_highlights.value: INR 11,217 crore; operating projects INR 7,183 crore
INR 3,463 crore pre-IPO; 3.24x; post-IPO net worth ~INR 5,200 crore

financial_highlights.change: Refinanced >INR 1,700 crore across three projects at <8%

qa_highlights.question: Does transmission delay pose a risk to the ~2 GW FY27 addition plan, and how is the TGNA route viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said >760 MW is already commissioned and the next ~300 MW is on STU with no grid issue. The remaining ~1 GW sits on operational substations; one ~300 MW substation should complete by December 2026. If CTU delays occur, batteries would be commissioned first and run merchant until GNA arrives.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and how much more spend is implied beyond 2,000 MW?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex was ~INR 16,000 crore as of 30 June 2026, rising to ~INR 22,000 crore by March 2027, covering ~3,900 MW commissioned by then plus CWIP for later capacity.

qa_highlights.question: How much curtailment hit Q1 and how is it being addressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Curtailment is ~2-2.5%, largely on the 50 MW Bikaner merchant plant on TGNA. Its 100 MWh battery is being doubled to 200 MWh within about a month; FDRE TGNA capacity has 400 MWh of battery, with more by October.

qa_highlights.question: What run-rate EBITDA applies to capacity added at March 2026 versus June 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Current 2,575 MW commissioned carries run-rate EBITDA of INR 1,620 crore; March 2026 capacity contributes INR 1,050 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the LOA-to-PPA conversion outlook given ~5 GW of LOAs against ~6 GW of PPAs?
qa_highlights.answer: Signed a 50 MW SJVN FDRE PPA; 550 MW of FDRE is unsigned, with 350 MW in advanced discussion with buyers confirmed and a 150 MW hybrid in very advanced talks. Management expects over 2 GW peak plus ~4 GWh BESS to be signed in the next few months, including the thermal-mimic tender.

qa_highlights.question: Where is BESS sourced, at what prices, and why is solar-plus-battery favoured over wind?
qa_highlights.answer: All ~4.5 GWh is contracted from Envision (AESC cells, PCS, EMS via Universe). Container prices were ~USD 59-60/kWh for ~2-3 GWh bought in January 2026, ~USD 65-68 now, and all-in ~USD 100-110/kWh. At ~USD 100-108/kWh, solar-plus-battery matches wind returns, so wind was cut to near-zero in newer projects.

qa_highlights.question: When can the SECI thermal-mimic project reach COD, and what are its module and transmission-charge assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Grid connectivity is already available in Rajasthan; COD follows PPA signing, with ~4,500 MW surplus connectivity. Module cost is INR 12.1-12.2/Wp non-DCR, with DCR modules assumed at ~INR 17/Wp; the ~75% CUF design is said to remove the transmission-charge waiver issue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT one-off and why was depreciation policy changed?
qa_highlights.answer: A ~INR 18 crore one-time refinancing cost hit PAT. Depreciation policy was aligned to market practice based on an external assessment; no quantified impact was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size and economics of merchant BESS, and what margins apply?
qa_highlights.answer: ~1.5 GWh not yet linked to projects will run merchant for 1-2 years; ~700 MWh more is due by December 2026. Charging costs ~INR 1-1.50/unit versus INR 2.50 earlier; some power sold on HPDAM at up to INR 20/unit. Standalone BESS is not pursued as returns are low; new tenders target higher-teens overall returns.

risks_watch: Transmission readiness: ~1 GW of CTU capacity and a ~300 MW substation due by December 2026 must land for the 2 GW FY27 target; 250-300 MW planned in Q2 FY27.
Conversion of LOAs to PPAs: ~550 MW FDRE and the 870 MW SECI thermal-mimic tender remain unsigned; COD depends on PPA signing.
BESS cost and supply: container prices rose from ~USD 59-60 to ~USD 65-68/kWh on lithium carbonate; all 4.5 GWh is from one vendor (Envision).
Merchant exposure: ~1.5 GWh of BESS will run merchant for 1-2 years, so earnings depend on daytime charging spreads and HPDAM prices.
Thermal-mimic operations: surplus of ~1-2% expected, no revenue assumed; also the 100 MWh to 200 MWh Bikaner battery upgrade must finish in about a month.
Capex rise from ~INR 16,000 crore to ~INR 22,000 crore by March 2027, with net debt of INR 11,217 crore and debt-to-equity of 3.24x pre-IPO.
key_quotes: We have delivered our highest ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA and the highest ever renewable capacity that we have commissioned in a single quarter.
What we have done is we are getting the PC S, the EMS, and the battery container from a single entity who provides this as a fully integrated single solution.
Now given the fact that solar plus battery is then easier to execute while not losing out on the returns, it makes common sense logic.
544853|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on execution, record commissioning and new tender wins, with the BESS and thermal-mimic economics explained in detail. Management was more cautious and vague on transmission timing, on the exact LOA-to-PPA conversion timing, and on the revenue split from BESS, which it said it could not separate from the renewable tariff.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin rose ~300 bps to 91% and operating margin ~400 bps to 90%; the 2,575 MW base carries INR 1,620 crore run-rate EBITDA and FY27 adds ~INR 2,750 crore, though BESS cost rises and merchant exposure (~1.5 GWh) weigh on the mix.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: FY27 (~2 GW to ~4 GW total); 250-300 MW in Q2 FY27; ~6 GW in
rows.why: 601 MWp commissioned in Q1 FY27 (record), >760 MW commissioned April to date, 250-300 MW targeted for Q2 FY27, and ~1.4 GW still needed within three quarters to reach the ~2 GW FY27 target.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Generation rose 72% to 944 million units and fleet CUF rose to 30.2% from 28.2%, with 601 MWp added in Q1 and 250-300 MW due in Q2 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex guided up from ~INR 16,000 crore to ~INR 22,000 crore by March 2027, with ~14,000 acres of land banked, >4.5 GW surplus connectivity and 200+ wind locations identified; fleet CUF 30.2% and ~6 GW FY28 plan imply further commitments.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 (~2 GW) and BESS (~4.5 GWh by June 2027, ~10 GWh by March 2028) targets rather than raising them, and cited tariff and BESS cost pressure (container prices ~USD 59-60 to ~USD 65-68/kWh).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Transmission timing is vague: ~1 GW CTU capacity and a ~300 MW substation due by December 2026 must land, and ~550 MW FDRE plus the 870 MW SECI thermal-mimic remain unsigned, so COD depends on PPA signing.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: ~400 MWh BESS commissioned in Q1, Bikaner battery doubling to 200 MWh within a month, ~700 MWh more merchant BESS due by December 2026, and ~10 GWh BESS targeted by March 2028.

rows.label: LOA-to-PPA conversion of ~550 MW FDRE and 870 MW SECI thermal-mimic
rows.why: Only a 50 MW SJVN PPA is signed; 350 MW is in advanced discussions and 150 MW hybrid in very advanced talks, and management expects over 2 GW peak plus ~4 GWh BESS to be signed in the next few months.

rows.label: Post-IPO balance sheet repair
rows.why: INR 1,800 crore IPO proceeds lift net worth to ~INR 5,200 crore from INR 3,463 crore, cutting net debt-to-equity from 3.24x, though net debt is INR 11,217 crore and capex rises to ~INR 22,000 crore.

rows.label: Refinancing to lower cost of debt
rows.why: More than INR 1,700 crore refinanced at <8% versus ~8.5% weighted average on the operational portfolio, with a ~INR 18 crore one-time cost already booked in Q1.

tone.note: Management was confident on record commissioning, tender wins and BESS targets, but cautious and vague on transmission timing, LOA-to-PPA conversion and the BESS revenue split; analysts pushed on the transmission path, PPA signing and the depreciation policy change.

544853|2026-09.headline: Juniper Green Q2 FY27 total income rose 2.3x YoY to INR 372 crores and EBITDA 2.6x to INR 340 crores, a record, at a 91.4% margin.
544853|2026-09.overview: Management reported a second consecutive record quarter, with total income of INR 372 crores (up 15% QoQ) and EBITDA of INR 340 crores (91.4% margin). Generation rose 127% YoY to 1,130 million units, with fleet CUF at 27% versus 21% a year earlier, and wind delivered 50% weighted CUF. Operational capacity reached 2.8 GWp plus 600 MWh BESS, with FY27 guidance of 2 GWp and 1.7 GWh BESS reiterated. Capex for the quarter was about INR 2,600 crores, and net debt to net worth improved to 2.22x after IPO proceeds, with ICRA upgrading the company to AA- stable.

financial_highlights.value: INR 54 crores (excl. refinancing and IPO one-time expenses)
financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR 18 crores in Q2 FY26; INR 53 crores adjusted in Q1 FY27
3.9x vs INR 40 crores in Q2 FY26
after INR 1,800 crores primary IPO proceeds; net debt to net worth 2.22x

financial_highlights.metric: Weighted average cost of debt (operational portfolio)
financial_highlights.change: from 8.58% last quarter; refinanced >INR 2,500 crores across 5 projects at below 8%

segments.name: Solar and wind generation (fleet)
segments.commentary: Q2 generation 1,130 MU (+127% YoY); fleet CUF 27% vs 21%. H1 generation 2,075 MU (+98%), H1 CUF 28.5% vs 24.1%. Wind weighted CUF 50% vs 41.3%; Juniper Green Beam (50 MW) at 58.3% CUF.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: About 100 MWh commissioned in Q2; about 500 MWh commissioned in first 7 months of FY27, taking operational BESS to 600 MWh. Operating assets report SOH above 99% and RTE near 90%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 commissioning guidance reiterated: 2 GWp generation capacity and 1.7 GWh BESS; about 3.9 GWp expected by March 2027.
EBITDA run rate: about INR 1,900 crores for the 2.8 GWp commissioned today; about INR 2,750 crores for the ~3.9 GWp expected by March 2027.
Total capex expected at about INR 24,000 crores by FY27 end, implying about INR 5,000 crores more in H2 on top of INR 19,000 crores cumulative to date.
Operational net debt expected to be close to INR 9,000 crores.
BESS installation targeted at about 4.5 GWh by June 2027 and 10 GWh by March 2028.
Projects slated for FY28 commissioning have dates not beyond June 2027 per management, about 6-9 months later than original dates.
About 1 to 1.3 GWp of the earlier ~4 GWp LOAs expected to convert to PSA/PPA within 1 to 1.5 months; thermal mimic PPA timing dependent on DISCOM selection.
capex_capacity: Operational capacity 2.8 GWp plus 600 MWh BESS across 11 sites in 3 states; 7-month FY27 additions of 494 MWp solar, 542 MW wind and about 500 MWh BESS.
Q2 commissioning about 316 MWp renewable plus about 100 MWh BESS, in line with 250-300 MWp guidance; total portfolio about 11.2 GWp plus 9 GWh BESS, of which 6.1 GWp operational or PPA-signed.
Envision E-182 turbines (5 MW, 181 m rotor, 130 m hub) — about 51 units commissioned.
Gross block INR 12,250 crores; CWIP incl. advances INR 6,600 crores; cumulative capex about INR 19,000 crores; H1 capex INR 3,800 crores.
Beta project: about 1,300 MWh merchant battery; about half expected operational by March 2027. Stellar project running on T-GNA; final line (Fatehgarh 3-Bhadla 3) expected December 2026.
demand_pricing: India power demand grew 10.2% in H1 FY27; management says standalone BESS arbitrage expected to continue as standalone BESS tenders have not materialised.
Q2 curtailment about 2.5% of revenue, concentrated in July-August before Stellar lines were completed; none in September-October per management, with batteries absorbing residual curtailment.
Battery prices expected to soften about 1-2% (from about INR 68-70 to INR 66-68 range) after China removed export incentive from January.
Non-DCR modules at about INR 12 or lower; DCR modules: SECI procurement at about INR 18, expected to be INR 18 or below in about a year.
Portfolio 86% contracted with central agencies (SJVN, NHPC, NTPC, SECI, GUVNL); 98% with offtakers rated A or above; 98% under long-term PPAs (typically 25 years); DSO 25 days.
Thermal mimic tender won: 230 MW contracted capacity, plan for 530 MW solar (1.5 DC ratio, ~790 MW DC), 75 MW wind and ~2.2 GWh BESS; management targets mid-to-high teens returns.

qa_highlights.question: Transmission risk, especially Juniper Green Stellar and Beta timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Stellar runs on T-GNA with one line (Fatehgarh 3-Bhadla 3, built by Apraava) expected in December 2026; Beta about half of its 1,300 MWh merchant battery expected by March 2027, with management confident of no curtailment even if slipping a couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: Operational net debt, Q2 CUF and capex plan for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Operational net debt close to INR 9,000 crores; Q2 CUF 27% and H1 28.5%; total capex to reach about INR 24,000 crores by FY27 end, with about INR 5,000 crores more in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Current EBITDA run rate and LOA-to-PPA conversion status?
qa_highlights.answer: Run rate about INR 1,900 crores for 2.8 GWp, rising to INR 2,750 crores for 3.9 GWp by March 2027. About 1-1.3 GWp of the earlier 4 GWp LOAs expected to move to PSA/PPA signing within 1-1.5 months; thermal mimic PPA delayed while DISCOMs select entities.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 projects avoid transmission delays and reach an EBITDA run rate of INR 4,300-4,400 crores by FY28-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give green shoots but said FY28 projects' transmission dates are no later than June 2027, 6-9 months behind original, and STU capacity is not hit by such delays, so it expects continued capacity expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Other income: components and sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly interest on surplus funds, with cash of INR 2,000 crores at 30 September; this income falls as cash is deployed into capex.

qa_highlights.question: Bidding strategy and return thresholds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets mid-to-high teens returns; it will skip aggressive solar-only tenders but bid tenders with batteries; standalone BESS bids on hold until tariffs correct.

qa_highlights.question: Thermal mimic returns and whether such tenders will recur?
qa_highlights.answer: Returns mid-to-high teens, versus about 20% on earlier 2023-24 FDRE bids that benefited from higher battery costs; management expects more such tenders.

risks_watch: Transmission delays: FY28 projects' lines already slipped 6-9 months; any further slip could push commissioning beyond June 2027.
LOA-to-PPA conversion: about 1-1.3 GWp expected in 1-1.5 months and thermal mimic PPA timing depends on DISCOM choice; watch signing.
Curtailment: Q2 about 2.5% of revenue; management says it has eased since September but depends on Stellar line completion and battery absorption.
Merchant BESS exposure: some batteries sold on short-tenor (1-6 month) DISCOM tenders until long-term PPAs are signed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 leasing of 4.4 mn sq ft (27 transactions) is about two-thirds of the 6.5 mn sq ft FY27 target, contracted revenue crossed INR1,004 crore, and a couple of mn sq ft of pre-commitments are to be delivered over the next 3-4 quarters, though Q3 is seasonally slower.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Land bank for 29-30 mn sq ft is fully paid with construction financing largely in place, speculative build is about two-thirds of the 6 mn sq ft target, and the acquisition engine is guided to restart in the next one to two quarters; utilisation is 94%, well above the 80% threshold.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated the 6.5 mn sq ft leasing target with 4.4 mn sq ft (about two-thirds) done in H1, but flagged Q3 seasonality from festivals and the mid-December to early-January shutdown, so no upgrade was signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Stabilised occupancy slipped to 94% from about 95%, Q3 leasing is seasonally slower, 0.7-0.8 mn sq ft of expiries land in H2 FY27, and the in-city Pune first lease and deliveries (Q4 FY27 / Q1 CY27) depend on execution and the CWC litigation remains sub judice.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First multi-story in-city Pune asset is due to deliver by Q4 FY27 / Q1 CY27 with first in-city lease targeted for Q3 FY27 at guided rents of INR60-90/sq ft (2-3x big-format parks), but the tenant and rent are confidential and in-city revenue is negligible today.

rows.label: Interest cost savings from post-IPO debt repayment
rows.why: About INR4,000 crore of debt was repaid at end-Q2, net debt fell to INR2,765 crore from INR4,967 crore, and cost of debt is about 8.2%, with the benefit guided to show mainly from Q3 and H1 impact negligible.

rows.why: About 38 MW is operational or under implementation against a 150-200 MW roof potential, with a planned 10 MW project at INR42-43 crore, but management said regulatory open-access approval is needed and gave no timeline.

rows.label: CWC litigation outcome

tone.note: Management was confident on leasing momentum, the 6 mn sq ft completion target and balance-sheet repair, but guarded on litigation, in-city rents (confidential) and solar scale; analysts pushed on the Q2 growth split and the occupancy dip to 94%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 55% YoY growth is volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes were approximately the same YoY, so growth came from product mix and customer relationships. No quantification was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin, given EBITDA of about 14% in Q1 after 9.5% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins move quarter to quarter with product mix and that the company focuses on profit amount rather than percentage. It did not commit to a sustainable margin range.

qa_highlights.question: How is gold price risk hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: The company buys gold equal to what it sells on the same day at market price. Inventory is carried at a weighted-average cost that management says is below market, so no hedging is needed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion comes from product mix and how much from inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mix was one factor and gold-price gains add 1-3 percentage points YoY. Analysts disputed that Q1 had gold gains, and management gave no split.

qa_highlights.question: How is growth funded and what is the working-capital cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Profits are reinvested, and the bank lines are open. The IPO raised equity to about INR450 crore to fund working capital. Management said the business needs more working capital as it grows.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers moving karigar work in-house, and what is the moat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said handcrafted, co-created bridal designs and long-standing relationships protect the business. It gave no figures to show the moat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did job-worker count fall and employee cost drop QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers larger, organised contract manufacturers. Employee cost fell because Q4 included an ex-gratia payment to directors, which will not recur.

544885|2026-06.headline: Gaja AMC Q1 FY27 PAT rose 35% YoY to INR27.2 crores; total income up 26% to INR51.8 crores.

Performance income of INR29.7 crores (+17% YoY) drove most of the income, while management fee income of about INR16 crores grew 7%. Cost-to-income improved to 38.4% from 42.3%. 544901|2026-06.headline: Purple Style Labs Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR119 crores (from INR106 crores), but EBITDA was negative INR11 crores vs negative INR4 crores a year earlier.
544901|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter with the four large-format experience centres opened in FY26 (Fort Mumbai, South Ex Delhi, Linking Road Bandra, Madison Avenue New York). GMV rose to INR193 crores from INR133 crores and AOV rose to INR86,000 from INR66,000. Revenue from operations was INR119 crores, gross margin held at 36%, and EBITDA and PAT losses were wider than a year earlier on the higher fixed cost base of the new stores. Inventory and net working capital fell year on year, but borrowings rose to INR436 crores at June 2026 from INR371 crores at FY26 end.

segments.name: Mumbai (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR50 crores from INR28 crores in the first three months of FY26. Mumbai was the largest market in FY26 GMV at INR205 crores.

segments.name: Delhi (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR39 crores from INR29 crores. Delhi FY26 GMV was INR166 crores.

segments.name: Hyderabad (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR16 crores from INR10 crores.

segments.name: USA (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR29 crores from INR20 crores. New York flagship opened in March 2026 and is the first US store; US was online-only before that.

guidance_outlook: No objective margin or profitability guidance given; management said it would refrain from it.
Q1 is the leanest quarter; management said the cost structure set in Q1 will carry into Q2 absent changes, and clearer trends are expected over the next two quarters.
No significant new experience centre expansion is planned near term; the first full year of the FY26 store investments is to be observed.

EBITDA break-even framing: on a P&L basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed for zero EBITDA, with lease-related costs of INR45 crores (lease interest plus ROU depreciation) included. On a cash basis, lease payments of INR29 crores imply a smaller gap.
Lease interest and ROU depreciation are expected to stay broadly flat unless stores change. Other finance cost should decline as operating profit reduces debt.
capex_capacity: Four large-format experience centres opened in FY26: Fort Mumbai and South Ex Delhi (operational since Q2 FY26), Linking Road Bandra (end-March 2026), and Madison Avenue New York (March 2026).
Store footprint is organised by geography, not by store, so same-store sales are not tracked. Mumbai now runs two large-format centres.
The New York lease is a June-end lease with a shorter tenure, so rent can be adjusted after 12-18 months of performance.
Inventory is expected to stay roughly flat at the current level absent further expansion. Management said inventory is around INR160 crores, with breadth-led singular-unit stock.
demand_pricing: AOV rose to INR86,000 in Q1 FY27, from INR76,000 in FY26 and INR46,000 in FY24. Store AOV is about 2.5x online AOV (India online about INR38,000 vs store about INR90,000 in FY26).
Active designer brands fell to 1,109 in FY26 from 1,910 in FY24. Top 100 designers were 67% of sales in FY24.
Average GMV per customer rose to INR108,000 in FY26 from INR67,000 in FY24. Top 50,000 customers contributed INR702 crores of FY26 GMV of INR722 crores.
Women's wear above INR1 lakh grew to INR312 crores GMV in FY26 from INR187 crores in FY24. Women's wear below INR35,000 fell to INR86 crores from INR162 crores.
Gross margin percentage is said to be broadly flat across price points. Management argued that absolute gross profit per piece rises with higher ticket size.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow still negative and borrowings rising despite lower inventory and working capital? When does the business become self-funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the lower inventory reflects better inventory management after the FY22-25 build-up, and higher customer advances (INR49 crores) helped working capital. Debt is funding interest costs, and Q1 is not operationally profitable. It asked investors to observe the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does the higher-ticket strategy improve gross margin or only AOV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said percentage gross margin is similar across categories. The benefit is in absolute gross profit per piece (e.g., at 40% margin a INR2 lakh piece yields INR80,000 vs INR8,000 for a INR20,000 piece), plus lower supply and customer complexity from the long tail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of outright purchase, consignment and backorder inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consignment split is business-sensitive and not disclosed. Outright purchase forms the inventory on the books. Backorder advances are about one month of revenue, and average delivery is 45-60 days, so backorder customer advances are not inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for finance costs in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Lease interest plus ROU depreciation (INR45 crores in the P&L) should stay at Q1 levels absent new store changes. Other finance cost should fall as operating profit reduces debt.

qa_highlights.question: What GMV scale, gross margin and operating leverage are needed for EBITDA positivity?
qa_highlights.answer: On an EBITDA basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed. Adding the lease costs of INR45 crores (P&L) or INR29 crores (cash) raises the required gross profit. Management referred to the detailed P&L on slide 20.

qa_highlights.question: What is the New York store's AOV and break-even, and what is the SSG for mature stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a New York store AOV of about INR1.25 lakh (about USD1,500), based on a 2.5x multiple to online AOV. It did not give a break-even GMV. Same-store growth is not tracked because the company reports by geography.

544903|2026-09.headline: Deepa Jewellers Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR 626 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.24% on plain-gold mix and PAT rose 37% to INR 37 crore.
544903|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 25% YoY to INR 626 crore, with EBITDA of INR 45 crore (up 17% YoY, margin 7.24%) and PAT of INR 37 crore (up 37%, margin 5.96%). H1 FY27 revenue rose 30% to INR 1,057 crore, EBITDA rose 24% to INR 84 crore (7.95% margin) and PAT rose 32% to INR 64 crore. Management attributed the Q2 growth moderation to festive demand shifting into H2, and said lower gross margin came from a plain-gold-heavy sales mix, with PAT supported by other income and a lower tax rate. The company also commenced its in-house Hyderabad manufacturing facility in September 2026 and guided to 40-45% revenue CAGR for FY27-FY29.

segments.name: Job work
segments.commentary: Volume of 318 kg in Q2 (+44% YoY) and 544 kg in H1 (+51% YoY). Realisation per gram fell to about INR 178-180 from about INR 200 a year earlier, which management attributed to plain-gold mix rather than pricing changes.

segments.name: Jewellery manufacturing (invoice/own gold)
segments.commentary: Volume of 491 kg in Q2 (broadly stable) and 783 kg in H1 (-5% YoY). Own-processing realisation fell to about INR 12,600/g from INR 14,500/g, attributed to lower gold prices, plain-gold mix and higher 18-karat sales.

segments.name: Studded vs plain gold mix
segments.commentary: Studded share was 57% of H1 FY27 sales, against 65% in FY26, with plain gold at 43%. Management targets studded share of 75% over the next three to four quarters.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of 40-45% guided for FY27, FY28 and FY29, with FY27 growth of 40-45% compared with FY26 (March 2026) base; the 40-45% figure was also described as a 40-50% revenue CAGR for two years at a constant 24-karat gold rate of INR 50,000.
EBITDA margin expected to expand 80-120 bps over the next 4-6 quarters, driven by the Hyderabad facility, Tier-2/3 expansion, studded mix and standalone store sales.
Gross margin pressure from plain-gold mix expected to normalise in upcoming quarters.
Hedging to rise from 94% toward close to 100% of gold holdings over the next two to three quarters.
Working capital cycle (inventory days plus receivable days) expected in the 55-65 day range; inventory and receivables expected to normalise from Q3.
Internal accruals, IPO proceeds and existing debt expected to fund growth through FY29.
Effective tax rate guided at the standard 25.168%; Q2 benefit came from deferred tax on IPO expenses, with the tax shield reversing in later years.
capex_capacity: In-house manufacturing facility in Hyderabad, about 6,700 sq ft, commenced operations in September 2026.
Facility capacity of about 1.5 tonnes a year on single shift and about 2.5 tonnes a year on double shift.
Facility processed 65 kg (13% of volume) in Q1 FY27 and 167 kg (21%) in Q2 FY27; management expects about 40% in Q3 and about 50% in Q4.
Second sales office in Chennai planned for December 2026; Bangalore office planned for April-May 2027, following Vijayawada office.
Long-run target mix of 65% in-house and 35% outsourced manufacturing; outsourced work to shift in-house from Q4 FY27.
demand_pricing: Revenue concentrated in South India (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala); client base about 373 customers including 47 jewellery retail chains such as Joyalukkas, Kalyan, Lalitha and Bhima.
Q2 growth moderated as festive demand shifted into H2; H1 typically contributes about 40% of annual revenue.
Retail customers shifting from cash purchases to old-gold exchange after a gold price spike, moving sales from invoice basis to job work; management said total volume shifted rather than fell.

Job work conversion margin is about 75% and invoice-basis about 8%, with a similar ROCE/ROE in both models; job work is priced at about 1% lower wastage (4% vs 5%) because it needs no working capital.
Gold price assumption for guidance: constant 24-karat rate of INR 50,000 per 10 g; average selling gold price rose from about INR 8,000/g in FY25 to INR 11,950/g in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin and grammage realisation decline in Q2, and why did job work realisation drop about 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the change was a shift toward plain gold jewellery (lower margin than studded), not a strategic or operational change, and expects normalisation. Job work realisation fell to about INR 178 from INR 202 a year earlier (about 11%), attributed to the same SKU mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory and receivable days rise versus March 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said March is not a like-for-like base because year-end corporate purchases stop; higher inventory came from stock built for the new Vijayawada sales office in September after IPO proceeds. Management expects normalisation from Q3 and a combined inventory plus receivable cycle of 55-65 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue outlook for the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth to come from new geographies (Vijayawada, Chennai, Bangalore offices), SKU expansion into studded casting, Nakshi and Tapa jewellery (16 SKUs launched in Q1), and client store expansion including franchise models. Guidance is 40-45% CAGR for FY27-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin impact of the new facility, and what EBITDA margin should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation and karigar costs weighed on Q1 and Q2 margins; benefit expected from Q3 as more volume shifts in-house. Management guided to an 80-120 bps EBITDA margin expansion over 4-6 quarters, with a note that studded mix and standalone store sales also contribute.

qa_highlights.question: How is gold price exposure hedged, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: 94% of gold holdings were hedged as of 30 September through gold metal loans (3.25% p.a.), MCX short futures and back-to-back unfixed purchases from bullion suppliers. Target is close to 100% within two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the effective tax rate fall to about 15%, and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the standard rate is 25.168%; the lower Q2 rate reflects deferred tax on IPO expenses, which Companies Act treats against securities premium while Income Tax allows over five years. The effect is expected to even out in later years.

qa_highlights.question: Will promoters draw salary, and how will they be compensated?
qa_highlights.answer: Both Ashish Agarwal and Dev Agarwal will not draw salary from 1 October 2026, and Dev Agarwal said no salary is planned for at least 10 quarters, after which the board will decide.

risks_watch: Gross margin and realisation pressure from plain-gold mix and lower gold prices; management quantified a 50% gold price fall at about 60 bps gross margin impact.
Working capital intensity: inventory and receivable days rose versus September FY26, and growth of 40-45% needs funding from accruals, IPO proceeds and debt.
Execution risk on new Hyderabad plant ramp-up (targeted about 40% of volume in Q3 and 50% in Q4) and on Chennai and Bangalore office launches.
Shift of retail customers toward old-gold exchange could keep invoice-basis sales subdued and raise job work share.
Customer concentration in South India and in a few large jewellery chains.
Tax rate normalisation from Q2 deferred benefit back to 25.168%.
Hedging coverage to rise to close to 100%; monitor in next quarter.
544903|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and margin recovery, with management repeatedly describing Q2 softness as a mix and timing effect. Management was more evasive on specifics, notably the EBITDA margin direction (a live misstatement of 80-120 bps versus a dip was clarified on the call) and on the basis for the 40-45% CAGR. Answers on the old-gold shift and inventory build were detailed and conceded the points.

It is just a change in the SKU mix which is expected to normalize in the upcoming quarters.
But yes, I accept that there has been a slight increase in the inventory days as well as the trade receivable days when we compare it to the numbers of September Fiscal '26.
So, over the next 4-5 quarters, we expect about 80-120 bps increase in our EBITDA margins over a period of next 4-6 quarters.

As of now, I as promoter of the company on a personal front have sufficient liquidity and as we are more inclined to the faster growth of the company, currently we have no plans of drawing any kind of salary at least for 10 quarters from now.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided 80-120 bps EBITDA margin expansion over 4-6 quarters from Hyderabad in-house shift, Tier-2/3 expansion and studded mix (57% of H1 sales vs 65% FY26, target 75% in 3-4 quarters), but Q2 margin fell to 7.24% and H1 margin is 7.95%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY27 onward (Chennai Dec 2026, Bangalore Apr-May 2027)
rows.why: Hyderabad facility commenced Sept 2026 (1.5 t/yr single shift, 2.5 t/yr double shift), with in-house share targeted at 40% of volume in Q3 and 50% in Q4 from 21% in Q2; Chennai office dated Dec 2026 and Bangalore Apr-May 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Total operating volume grew 13% YoY to 809 kg in Q2 and 12% to 1,327 kg in H1, with job work up 44% in Q2; processing/manufacturing was flat (-5% in H1), and festive demand is expected in H2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed; the single-shift Hyderabad plant has 1.5 t/yr capacity with 167 kg processed in Q2, and the company plans a 65% in-house target, so further capacity could be needed, but no new capex was guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 revenue growth slowed to 25% YoY from H1's 30%, and the 40-45% CAGR is not tied to specific orders, so there is no sign of a guidance raise yet.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Growth decelerated from 30% in H1 to 25% in Q2, the Hyderabad ramp (21% to 50% of volume by Q4) and working capital (55-65 day cycle) are execution risks, and the 40-45% CAGR is not backed by specific orders.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Studded casting, Nakshi and Tapa jewellery SKUs were launched (16 SKUs in Q1), and management cited SKU expansion as a growth driver, but no specific new launch dates were given beyond those.

rows.label: Inventory plus receivable cycle back to 55-65 days
rows.why: Management said inventory and receivables will normalise from Q3 and expects a combined cycle of 55-65 days, with higher inventory tied to stock built for the Vijayawada office after IPO proceeds.

rows.label: Gold hedging rising to near 100%
rows.why: Hedging rose to 94% of gold holdings at 30 September from 75% over 2-3 years, with a stated aim of close to 100% in 2-3 quarters, which cuts price risk.

rows.label: Gross margin normalisation from plain-gold mix
rows.why: Job work realisation fell to about INR 178/g from about INR 200/g and own-processing to INR 12,600/g from INR 14,500/g; management expects normalisation, but a 50% gold price fall would cut gross margin about 60 bps.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 40-45% CAGR, the Hyderabad ramp and margin recovery, and described Q2 softness as mix and timing; analysts pressed on the margin direction, the basis for the CAGR, the low tax rate, and the inventory build.

544911|2026-06.headline: Kanohar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 103.5% YoY to INR137.1 crore, with EBITDA margin of 28.3% and order book of about INR2,026 crore.
544911|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR137.1 crore, up 103.5% YoY, with transformers at 84.9% and EPC at 14.81% of revenue. EBITDA rose 152.2% to INR38.8 crore (28.3% margin, up 550 bps) and PAT rose 140% to INR27.3 crore (19.9% margin). Consolidated order book stood at about INR2,026 crore on June 30, 2026, up 11% from March 31, 2026, after incremental orders of INR332.2 crore in Q1 and INR867.3 crore in Q2 to date. financial_highlights.value: Q1: INR332.2 crore; Q2 to date: INR867.3 crore

segments.name: Power Transformers / 400 kV
segments.commentary: 400 kV transformers contributed 70.16% of Q1 revenue (52% in FY26, 10.3% in FY24). Management said 400 kV, Scott-connected and shunt reactor products carry similar gross margins; about 70% of order book is power transformers, mostly 400 kV.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: EPC contributed 14.81% of Q1 revenue. Management does not disclose EBITDA separately; directionally lower than transformer margins.

segments.name: By end-user
segments.commentary: Power Transmission 85.18%, Railways 11.53%, Renewable Energy 2.84%, Power Distribution 0.23% of Q1 revenue. Shunt reactors were about 13.1% of order book at June 30.

segments.name: Voltage mix (other)
segments.commentary: 132 kV to below 220 kV at 11.38%, 220 kV to below 400 kV at 3.19%, below 132 kV at 0.23% of Q1 revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about INR950 crore, with EBITDA margin broadly similar to FY26.
FY28 revenue growth expected to be similar to FY27 guidance (about 40-45% per analyst's read, not confirmed by management).
Brownfield expansion of about 18,000 MVA at Gangol, targeted to be in place by end-FY28 / FY29; existing capacity seen sufficient through FY28.
Net working capital guided at 110-120 days.
Order book at end-FY27 may be adequate to cover FY28 and FY29 revenue, per management; no specific FY27 closing order book number given.
Shunt reactors expected to be about 10-15% of revenue on average over time.
capex_capacity: Existing capacity about 19,200 MVA across Rithani and Gangol (Meerut); Gangol about 18,000 MVA.
Q1 FY27 executed about 1,725 MVA, implying roughly 36-46% utilisation depending on base used.
Planned brownfield expansion of about 18,000 MVA at Gangol; part funded from IPO proceeds.
765 kV: technology developed in-house; capacity to be suitable for 765 kV; management estimates 3-4 years to become eligible for regular 765 kV tenders.
About 2,500 kW solar plant planned, partly funded from IPO proceeds; savings not quantified.
demand_pricing: Management estimates India 400 kV transformer market at about 60,000-70,000 MVA last year, growing 10-15% industry-wide; analyst's INR4,000-6,000 crore 400 kV market size was confirmed as 'in that range'.
Railways envisages about 1,000 traction substations for high-speed rail over 5-10 years (about 2,000 transformers), implying about INR20,000 crore opportunity.
Most contracts have price variation clauses (IEEMA PVC), which management says offsets raw material swings; order book margins said to be similar to FY26.
Industry lead times are 18-24 months; tenders being bid are mainly for FY29-FY30 execution.
Revenue per MVA about INR6.1 lakh last year; may have risen slightly due to raw material costs.
Management said there were no new entrants in the last 3-6 months that it is aware of, but expects new entrants over time.

qa_highlights.question: How were transformer margins protected in Q1 given input cost increases and fixed-price contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most contracts carry price variation linked to the IEEMA clause, which passes through raw material moves in both directions.

qa_highlights.question: Will GEC-III drive a multi-year order tailwind for 400 kV and 500 MVA transformers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a multi-decadal structural tailwind; intra-state transmission is mostly 400 kV, but no split of GEC-III capacity by voltage was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can order book reach INR3,000 crore by FY27 end, and 40-45% YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to confirm; said Q2 execution will reduce the order book slightly, and end-FY27 book may cover FY28-FY29 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1H-weak, 2H-heavy revenue pattern a continuing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said H1 is typically softer and H2 heavier, an industry trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will new 400 kV capacity pressure margins beyond 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects visibility for 3-4 years from current order book and tenders; beyond that, short-term supply-demand mismatch and margin pressure are possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY24 a revenue decline and why is utilisation low; are exports planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY24 focus went to obtaining 400 kV and Scott certifications; ramp-up takes time. Exports are not the current focus; a re-look may come in 3-4 years.

risks_watch: Supply chain and raw material availability, which management named as the key risk; geopolitical sourcing issues were raised.
Margin pressure from new 400 kV entrants and added capacity beyond the 3-4 year visibility window.
Execution timing: H2-weighted revenue and 18-24 month execution cycles.
Capacity addition: brownfield 18,000 MVA must come on stream by FY28-FY29 to support growth.
Order book lumpiness toward power transformers, with large CPSU orders (INR250 crore+) in Q2.
Working capital intensity of 110-120 net days.
Management did not disclose bid pipeline, EBITDA by segment, or the MVA-based breakdown beyond Q1 execution.

Right now, we are seeing a stable margin profile.

544912|2026-09.headline: Prasol Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR413 crore (+38.6% YoY) and EBITDA INR58 crore (+86.1%), with FY27 guidance reiterated.

H1 FY27 EBITDA of INR148 crore included a one-time INR25 crore inventory gain and INR0.92 crore forex gain in Q1, and management said underlying full-year EBITDA should be INR240-250 crore. Working capital cycle lengthened from 63 to 76 days as the company added shorter-credit suppliers, and H1 operating cash flow was negative.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has a formula-based pricing arrangement with its top 10 customers and books inventory only against order visibility. Price cuts are passed on with a 15-30 day lag, so the company is exposed when prices fall and benefits when they rise.

qa_highlights.question: Why is H1 operating cash flow negative, and what is the full-year outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said H1 cash flow is a snapshot and the working capital build reflects new suppliers, higher inventory cost and longer shipping times. Management expects inventory to normalise by end Q3 and expects to rebuild inventory in Q4 if demand holds.

qa_highlights.question: What are plant utilisation levels and which industries are targeted by expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined utilisation of both plants is about 65-75%. Expansions cover every non-agro product, with increases of 30-100%. Forward integration and identical plants for lubricant grades are planned.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO said growth came from higher realisations, with single-digit volume growth in the domestic business.

544913|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 16% to Rs.239 crores and EBITDA rose 22% to Rs.60 crores at a 25.3% margin; FY27 guidance held.

Order book stood at Rs.957 crores at September 30, 2026, with management targeting Rs.500 crores-plus of new bookings in Q3-Q4 to hold about 18 months of visibility. Israel is a new market, with a first job expected below Rs.50 crores.

segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.22 crores, up 82% YoY, which management said reflects project execution rather than a run-rate. Management expects substantial bookings in Q3-Q4 and says the segment carries higher margins.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-22%, unchanged from the previous call.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 23-25% and PAT margin at 18-20%, both unchanged.
Q3-Q4 expected to be much stronger; an analyst extrapolation of over 30% H2 top-line growth was described as ballpark accurate by management.
Target of Rs.500 crores-plus of new order bookings in Q3-Q4 to end FY27 with about 18 months of visibility.
Glass processing unit commissioning expected July-August 2027, with an estimated 1-1.5% EBITDA margin benefit from Q3-Q4 FY28.
Working capital days guided at around 45 days, with anything below that described as a bonus.
capex_capacity: Glass processing unit project cost is about Rs.70-odd crores, funded from IPO proceeds held separately. Civil construction is expected to finish in 2-3 months, machinery arrival in 6-7 months, and commissioning in 2-3 months.

demand_pricing: Order book of Rs.957 crores at September 30, 2026, against Rs.846 crores at April 2026 and Rs.383 crores at the start of FY26. Management expects to execute about Rs.350 crores over the next two quarters and says the book will run for 18-24 months.

Management says it is choosing jobs on client, terms, margin and execution period rather than chasing win ratio, and that it could win all Rs.3,000 crores of pipeline by cutting prices about 5%.

Q2 wins included a Mumbai hotel job of about Rs.90 crores and two South India data-centre jobs of about Rs.35-40 crores. Management expects data centres to be a few jobs only, with hospitality and commercial as stronger segments.

qa_highlights.question: Are US customers cancelling existing orders, or is the Q3-Q4 strength tied to new orders?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp Q2 margin increase on flat revenue?

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.500 crores order target for Q3-Q4 alone, and what is the split across segments?

qa_highlights.question: How do aluminium and glass price changes flow through?

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20-22% growth guidance net of freight, and what is the freight mechanism?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Israel and US new-client wins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a first Israel order in Q3-Q4 FY27, initially below Rs.50 crores, with larger jobs possible within 1.5-2 years. It said the US bids cover both existing and new clients, with a couple of awards possible in the next quarter.

544914|2026-06.headline: Steamhouse Q1 FY27 PAT rose 80.25% YoY to INR18.34 crore on 16.7% steam volume growth; EBITDA margin 24.05%.
544914|2026-06.overview: Steamhouse reported record quarterly steam volumes of about 3,05,816 tons, up 16.7% YoY and 11.52% QoQ, with revenue from operations up 13.35% to INR128.62 crore. EBITDA rose 60.08% to INR30.93 crore, lifting margin to 24.05% (up 702 bps), while PAT rose 80.25% to INR18.34 crore. Management attributed the gains to higher volumes, utilisation (41.40% vs 36.06% YoY) and operating leverage, and noted the exit from low-margin coal trading. Gross debt rose to INR359.48 crore from INR281.62 crore at FY26 end, with IPO proceeds earmarked for debt reduction and capacity expansion.

segments.commentary: Traded steam was 22.2% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Coal trading has been discontinued as low-margin; two trading agreements (Dahej SEZ, Haldia) are signed and management declined to split margins between generation and trading.

segments.commentary: PSA-based nitrogen plant of 350 Nm3/hr commissioned at Ankleshwar. Management described it as currently small and plans air separation units for LIN/LOX and other gases.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in the business across quarters, and what explains the Q1 volume jump over Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no real consumption seasonality, but monsoon is challenging (wet fuel, flooded industrial clusters). Q1 volume growth was attributed to chemical and pharma demand recovering and repeat customers.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the 345 TPH capacity is contracted, and can customers terminate contracts early?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of the 345 TPH installed capacity is tied up under contracts. Tenure ranges 1 to 10 years with non-exit clauses, and management said customers rarely move to captive boilers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value proposition to win customers from competitors or in-house boilers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is generally no competitor in most geographies. Claimed cost saving versus captive furnace oil, LDO or natural gas is 25% to 35%, while coal-fired large textile users may be only at par.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is needed to reach 705 TPH and when will projects go live?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR60 crore more for the four under-construction projects, targeted to go live in FY27. Another INR170 crore over 15-18 months for IPO-funded and Tarapur projects; Tarapur 60 TPH by Q4 FY28, Dahej/Ankleshwar/Panoli by Q1 FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is utilisation of 41% consistent with the planned ramp, and where does the company target it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 60%-65% utilisation; newer boilers are expected to run at about 50% in initial months after commissioning. Some capacity is held back for 2-3 years of new demand.

qa_highlights.question: What are receivable days and CFO to EBITDA ratio, and what are the related-party steam purchases from Sanjoo Dyeing?
qa_highlights.answer: Fortnightly billing with payments typically 7th to 15th day. Operating cash flow was about 1.2 times EBITDA last time, expected to hold or be slightly lower. Steam purchases from Sanjoo Dyeing for the Sachin location continue for at least the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected on the Una project and what is the revenue-share structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 8%-10% clear margin per ton, passed through to end consumers, with no capex. The 9% revenue share to Himachal Pradesh Bulk Drug Park Infrastructure Ltd is to be recovered from steam customers. Agreement not yet signed.

qa_highlights.question: What is a sustainable volume growth rate and can company-level 20%-25% volume growth be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 5%-10% growth at existing locations, with new capacity adding further. CFO said 20%-25% company-level volume growth is achievable 'very comfortably'.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR1,000 EBITDA per ton sustainable, and what about Q2 seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA per ton of about INR1,000 is expected to hold for the next few quarters, with Q2 an exception due to monsoon. Structural changes cited: coal purchases moved from credit to cash, solar power installed, inventory optimisation. Full-year to be at par or better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there government interest in community boilers and are more such opportunities in the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to Bulk Drug Park and PM MITRA Park schemes from 2021-22 and a March 2024 CPCB guideline pushing SMEs to common boilers. Gujarat Bulk Drug Park tender is live; PM MITRA and Textile Ministry discussions are ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did steam revenue rise 46% when volume rose 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation improved from better utilisation and asset leverage, plus higher waste-to-energy usage at Vapi. Growth also came from chemical and pharma recovery and new tyre and food processing (Haldia) customers.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital guidance and cash purchases?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle guided at 35-40 days positive. Coal was bought on credit until May 2026 and has since moved entirely to cash purchases, which management said lowers fuel cost.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split between own-generated and traded steam, and margin split by business?
qa_highlights.answer: Own-boiler steam was 73.7% of Q1 revenue and traded steam 22.2%. Management declined to split margins between generation and trading, citing competitive sensitivity.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will try to maintain the Q1 growth momentum for the full year on both EBITDA and revenue, but said 'We are not saying that we will maintain'.

544914|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 steam sales were 3,01,642 tons, up 12.06% YoY but down about 1.36% QoQ, with monsoon conditions and one steam supplier's shutdown cited as drags. Revenue from operations was INR128 crore (up 2.4% YoY) and EBITDA was INR24.68 crore, with margin at 19.28% against 11.39% a year earlier. Sequentially, EBITDA fell from INR30.93 crore in Q1 and EBITDA per ton declined, which management attributed to monsoon-related fuel wetness, transmission losses and cost movements. H1 FY27 steam sales rose 14.35% YoY, and management reiterated 25% FY27 volume growth and 35% growth in FY28, with an EBITDA per ton target of INR1,100-1,200 for the next full year.

segments.name: Steam generation and distribution
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue from steam generation and distribution was INR96.97 crore; steam distribution contributed INR25.56 crore. Own generation was 2,31,775.59 tons and steam purchase/distribution was 69,866.67 tons in Q2.

segments.name: Nitrogen and other
segments.commentary: Balance of Q2 revenue (about INR5.5 crore) came from nitrogen and other items; nitrogen is billed per nm3 per hour, not per ton. A 750 nm3/hour PSA plant at Ankleshwar is expected by end-CY2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 steam volume growth target of about 25% over FY26's 10.66 lakh tons, implying about 13.25 lakh tons; H2 must grow about 35% YoY versus H1 to hit this.
FY28 volume growth expected to be upwards of 35%, driven by new facilities and customers added in FY27.
Next full year EBITDA per ton guided at INR1,100-1,200, supported by waste-to-steam facilities; Q3 and Q4 expected to be significantly higher than Q2 as the dry season reduces fuel losses.
Quarterly interest cost guided to be a little below the approx INR6 crore run-rate in Q3, as IPO proceeds repaid part of the debt raised in Q1.
Jhagadia steam sales expected to start in November 2026; Nandesari and Vapi waste-to-steam plants expected in H2 FY27; a third waste-to-steam plant expected in the next calendar year.
capex_capacity: Jhagadia: about 14.8 tons per hour contracted out of 30 tons per hour planned; commissioning expected imminently.

Nandesari and Vapi expansions progressing; Vapi is about 7-8 km from existing facility and includes a roughly 1.5 km pipeline. Tarapur and Pirana under construction (Pirana targeting textile cluster in Ahmedabad).

Una (Himachal Pradesh) community boiler: 300 tons per hour, EPC mandate of about INR311 crore incl. GST plus long-term O&M; funded by Himachal Pradesh Bulk Drug Park Infrastructure Limited; pricing still under negotiation.
Waste-to-steam capex is about 1.5x-1.75x coal-fired projects on a like-for-like capacity basis, with opex about 50-55% lower; management cites a 2.5-3.5 year payback after stabilisation.
Capacity utilisation: 42.41% in Q2 FY27 vs 35.28% in Q2 FY26 and 41.40% in Q1 FY27; H1 FY27 at 41.91% vs 37.03%.
demand_pricing: Steam volumes grew 14.35% YoY in H1 FY27 to 6,07,459 tons (5,31,240 tons in H1 FY26); 99.48% of H1 FY27 revenue came from repeat customers.
Steam prices were raised about 17-18% from Q1 to Q2 and the pass-through of coal price changes is contractual, with a lag of around 15 days.
Fuel: imported Indonesian 4,200 GCV coal at about INR10,000-10,500 per ton as of the call, up from INR9,000-10,000 earlier and a temporary INR10,500-11,000 peak at end-September.
New sectors being added include food processing and adhesives, on top of the chemical, agrochemical and pharma base; Narol textile cluster targeted via Pirana.
Management said it is evaluating a large waste-based steam project in Sachin GIDC targeting the textile cluster, which is price sensitive.

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth is expected for H2 FY27 and FY28 based on current contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target is about 25% volume growth over 10.66 lakh tons in FY26; FY28 volume growth is expected to be upwards of 35%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per ton fall from about INR1,000 to about INR818 QoQ, and what is coal cost and interest outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop to monsoon-related wet coal, higher transmission losses and cost movements; coal is a pass-through. Quarterly interest expected to be slightly below about INR6 crore in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA per ton is expected from the Himachal Pradesh (Una) EPC project given the 9% government revenue share and imported coal transport?

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% volume growth realistic given Q2 margin decline, and what EBITDA margin is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is on track for both volume growth and EBITDA margin, and reiterated that Q2 is a seasonally soft quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How do trade payables and negative operating cash flow look going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Trade payables were largely cleared early using IPO money to earn cash discounts; payables are expected to remain in single digits, so operating cash flow should normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What are the penalty clauses for supply shortfalls?
qa_highlights.answer: Most agreements are supply-subject-to-availability with no penalty; some have quarterly minimum guarantees (for example 60% of contracted capacity), and no penalty has been paid historically.

risks_watch: Q3 and Q4 delivery of the guided EBITDA per ton ramp depends on waste-to-steam plant commissioning timelines (Jhagadia, Nandesari, Vapi and a further plant next calendar year).
Volume growth needs H2 FY27 to grow about 35% over H1; any further supplier shutdown or monsoon disruption would slow this.
Coal price pass-through lag (about 15 days) and an enlarged gap between steam revenue growth and volume growth can distort margins.
Return ratios are diluted after the IPO: ROCE of 12.97% and ROE of 4.53% (not annualised).
Himachal Pradesh project: offtake is not committed by the government and pricing is still under negotiation.
Operating cash flow was negative in H1 and trade payables were largely cleared; management expects payables to stay in single digits.

key_quotes: Both in terms of EBITDA margin and in terms of volume growth, we are very much on track and we are confident.
Q2 is going to be soft in the going years, upcoming years as well.

544916|2026-06.headline: MPi H1 FY27 revenue rose 40.3% to INR 849.4 crore and PAT 45.4% to INR 158.6 crore, while Q2 operational EBITDA margin fell to 30.5%.
544916|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 33.6% to INR 430.4 crore in Q2 FY27 and 40.3% to INR 849.4 crore in H1. Emerging businesses grew 92% in H1 and reached 34.5% of revenue, while core business grew 23%. Operational EBITDA rose 17.5% in Q2 to INR 131.3 crore, with margin at 30.5%, held back by forex, input costs and freight. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 30-35% and a 25% CAGR for FY27-29.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 294 crore in Q2 (+23% from INR 239 crore) and INR 556 crore in H1 (+23%). Growth driven by higher domestic card volumes, a new debit card logistics mandate from a large PSU bank, and transit card projects.

segments.name: Emerging business (international cards, metal cards, tax stamps, RFID)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 136 crore in Q2 (+63% from INR 84 crore) and INR 293 crore in H1 (+92%). Share of revenue was 31.7% in Q2 versus 25.9% a year ago. Metal cards and tax stamps are described as margin-accretive.

segments.name: International operations (Nigeria, UK, other regions)
segments.commentary: Nigeria bureau started in Q1 and added more than 10 customers in Q2 (over 20 in H1 per management). UK personalisation bureau is now operational, with revenue expected in H2 FY27.

FY27-FY29 revenue CAGR of about 25% indicated.

UK bureau expected to contribute revenue from H2 FY27; one more large developed market to be set up by end of FY27.

Asset life of machines is 7, 10 and 15 years depending on type.

Global PVC card issuance is growing 2-4% YoY and metal cards about 15% annualised, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 EBITDA margin rise sequentially while emerging revenue fell QoQ, and what is the H2 pipeline for exports and metal cards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed margin movement to sales and product mix, with a quarter-on-quarter variation expected. It said order timing varies by quarter, and that it is confident of the international guidance for H2. It did not quantify metal card or tax stamp mix.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw material import costs passed through to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: PSU contracts are fixed for 2-3 years (sometimes 5) with force majeure renegotiation. Private banks, cooperative banks and fintechs can be renegotiated. Management said pricing factors in variances.

qa_highlights.question: Why did freight cost roughly double YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight is a direct cost tied to the integrated logistics business, which delivers cards end-to-end to customer beneficiaries. It rises with bundled service volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why has depreciation risen sharply, and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation rose to INR 22.4 crore in Q2 from INR 11.9 crore due to leased assets on five-year tenures. Management expects it to normalise as INR 240 crore of IPO-funded capex comes in.

qa_highlights.question: What are the UK and US opportunities and timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: The UK business is with the largest new UK bank and revenue is expected in H2. US sales teams are in place and some revenue is hoped for this year. Management would not name large bank breakthroughs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the utilisation and how will international expansion be supported?
qa_highlights.answer: Plastic card capacity is about 80%, metal 55-60%, and tax stamps 70-75%. Capacity is not seen as a constraint given the INR 240 crore capex plan.
