544917|2026-06.headline: Karamtara Q1 FY27 revenue rose 72% YoY to INR1,581 crore, EBITDA INR174 crore (~11% margin), PAT INR87 crore; FY27 growth target 60-65%.
544917|2026-06.overview: Karamtara's first call as a listed company reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of INR1,581 crore (+72% YoY), EBITDA of INR174 crore (+45% YoY, ~11% margin) and PAT of INR87 crore (+45% YoY). Management said the quarter was hit by elevated freight and tariff-related costs, which it expects to ease, and reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 60-65%. Transmission was flagged as the next major growth driver, with new Bhachau capacity ramping and a Saudi Arabia plant targeted for trials around December. Management gave no FY28 numbers and no explicit margin guidance.

segments.name: Renewables (solar, wind, transmission)
segments.commentary: Renewable products were 82% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management said transmission (about 30% of revenue per an analyst's reading) is the next major growth driver.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: Solar revenue grew from about INR20 crore in FY21 to an expected INR5,000-5,500 crore this year, per management. Portfolio includes module mounting structures, tracker piles, torque tubes, couplers, purlins and stamp parts.

segments.name: Transmission
segments.commentary: New Bhachau facility began manufacturing recently; management expects peak capacity within 6-9 months. Lattice towers up to 1,200 kV.

segments.name: PEB (data centre)
segments.commentary: New PEB facility at Bhachau expected to start by the beginning of next financial year, with revenue in FY28 and a larger share after that.

segments.name: Fasteners
segments.commentary: Bolts, nuts, studs and washers for solar, wind, transmission, bridges and railways. Facility moved to Nagpur after a rolling mill there was shut down.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of 60-65% YoY; management said it hopes to beat this internally.
Revenue seasonality: 40-42% in H1 and 58-60% in H2, per management's historical pattern.
EBITDA margin expected to improve as utilisation rises and fixed costs are absorbed; no numerical margin guidance given. Management cited freight normalisation as a further lever.

Saudi Arabia plant: trials around December, galvanizing plant online by February or March, commercial output by end-CY/early next year; 12-18 months to reach strong utilisation; revenue begins next year.
No FY28 revenue guidance; management said strong growth is expected from Saudi, PEB and transmission capex.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity of 889,200 MTPA as of quarter end, excluding captive rolling and galvanizing capacity.
13 manufacturing facilities: 8 in Maharashtra (7 Boisar, 1 Nagpur), 4 in Gujarat (Bhachau), 1 in Italy.
New Bhachau rolling mill for transmission towers and solar tracker piles now ramping; management expects peak capacity in 6-9 months.
Under construction: PEB facility at Bhachau (data centres), solar stamped parts facility at Boisar, multiproduct plant in Saudi Arabia (transmission and solar).
Capex of about INR900 crore in FY26 and continued investment in FY27; management said capex is funded partly by IPO proceeds, with some term loan debt.
demand_pricing: Management said demand continues to outpace supply in the renewables market; large installed capacity allows selective order acceptance.

Contracts: Indian solar contracts run 4-5 months with steel and zinc covered by mill credit (~90 days). Export contracts run 8-9 months with imported raw material. Management says commodity risk is passed through to customers via pass-through or price-variation clauses.

US: steel and aluminium products face a 50% Section 232 tariff, which management says was fully passed through to buyers. US domestic supply of these products is limited; management said local US prices are 30-40% above Indian landed prices, with 6-8 month lead times.
Freight and shipping costs are at elevated levels globally because of fuel prices, which weighed on Q1 margins.
No major real competition from Indian companies in US exports, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Strategy on business mix and transmission share, given strong bidding and pricing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said transmission will be a very large growth driver, citing the new Bhachau facility, hybrid wind towers that can be switched to transmission, and the Saudi plant. It plans to build the transmission portfolio as it did solar.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 trend and FY27 guidance on revenue and EBITDA margin.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 has been good and reiterated 60-65% growth for FY27 with H1 at 40-42% of revenue. It said margins will rise with utilisation but gave no numerical guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Contract structure: cost-plus, fixed or mixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic solar contracts are 4-5 months and export contracts 8-9 months, with raw material pass-through. Long-term domestic transmission and some export contracts have price-variation clauses; some large overseas FOB contracts pass shipping through.

qa_highlights.question: Would tariffs erode US export competitiveness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 50% steel tariff under Section 232 is fixed and any further tariffs do not stack. Tariff costs were passed through to buyers, and US buyers face 30-40% higher local prices.

qa_highlights.question: Margin lever: product mix, Saudi or operating leverage? Utilisation path to 75%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will improve as assets are utilised and fixed costs are absorbed, with local-content Saudi output expected to earn better margins. Bhuj and Saudi ramps will take 6-18 months, and the company expects growth to come from all segments.

qa_highlights.question: PEB differentiation and expected margins.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the entry is aimed at data-centre demand, with qualification in the Nordics and existing customer pull. It declined to commit to a margin range but expects margins similar to its other businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Tariff-adjusted revenue comparison.
qa_highlights.answer: Tariff pass-through was about INR250 crore in Q1 FY27 versus about INR113 crore in Q1 FY26 and about INR196 crore in the prior quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Volume and other expenses.
qa_highlights.answer: Volume was about 135,000 tonnes. Other expenses of about INR500 crore include tariff and freight costs, which management said are passed on to customers.

544921|2026-09.headline: ARCIL H1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 54% to INR290 crores on 48% higher total income of INR516 crores; acquisitions up 18% to INR1,707 crores.
544921|2026-09.overview: ARCIL reported H1 FY27 (six months to September 30, 2026) with AUM up 21% to INR20,274 crores and total income up 48% to INR516 crores. Q2 acquisitions reached INR1,354 crores, up 43% year on year, after a weak Q1 of INR353 crores, consistent with the seasonal pattern management described. Q2 recoveries of INR1,069 crores were below the strong prior-year Q2 that included large corporate resolutions, and an ECL provision taken in Q1 was partly reversed in Q2. Management asked investors to judge the company on standalone results and over longer periods, and gave no numerical guidance.

segments.name: Corporate acquisitions
segments.commentary: About INR700 crores of the H1 acquisitions were corporate; the remaining about INR1,000 crores were SME and retail. Corporate AUM is about INR13,000 crores.

guidance_outlook: No numerical guidance on AUM, acquisitions or H2 profitability; management pointed to historical performance and regularity of recoveries.
Management said H2 is seasonally the stronger acquisition period, with about 60% of last year's acquisitions in H2, and described the pipeline as healthy.
Write-backs are expected to be lower in H2 than in H1, but will remain a recurring part of revenue.
Investment upsides have run at INR200 crores-plus a year for the last 2-3 years, and management expects a consistent flow.
Management said fee plus investment upside should be about 70-80% of total revenue over time, with management fee run-rate of about INR450 crores per annum.
Collection-as-a-service pilots with a couple of lenders are expected to scale in H2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Borrowings rose to INR1,224 crores to fund Q2 acquisitions; management said the balance sheet can fund H2.
ARCIL invested INR718 crores of its own capital in H1 acquisitions, an investment ratio of 42% (33% last year).

Priorities include growing mid-sized corporate assets, raising retail and SME share, scaling collection as a service, and selectively evaluating stressed microfinance portfolios.
demand_pricing: Management estimates total stress at about INR23.7 lakh crores (CRISIL, FY26), of which about INR15.9 lakh crores is NPAs and written-off loans; ARCs buy below 10% of the pool annually per management's internal estimate.
Unsecured retail assets were acquired at single-digit percent of dues and secured retail at mid-40s percent, per management.
Management said about 70% of the last two years' acquisitions were on an AUM basis, and that the majority of H1 acquisitions were structured SR deals rather than cash deals.
Management said ARCs do not currently participate in agri or gold loan stress; microfinance is being evaluated selectively.
Management said competition from NARCL is focused on very large assets, and ARCIL differentiates by covering all asset classes.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors model lumpy non-fee revenue such as upsides and writebacks across the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said large corporate recoveries are lumpy but recur because of the large corporate book, so regularity should be judged rather than single items. Writebacks were INR125 crores in Q1 and lower in Q2, totalling INR140 crores for H1, and are expected to be lower in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ECL impairment reverse in Q2, and what is the sustainable level?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the ECL provision is quarter-to-quarter, rising when receivables increase, as in Q1, and partly reversed in Q2. Annual ECL provisioning under RBI rules is about INR15-20 crores, which he called unsubstantial.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fee income grow 82% against 21% AUM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income comes from acquisitions and also includes collection-based fees, so it depends on both AUM and collections. Quarterly fee income has stabilised at about INR115-120 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Are there signs of stress and competitive intensity affecting the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the existing stress pool of over INR23 lakh crores is large enough for growth, and that ARCIL is positioned with 0.37x debt-to-equity and 70.5% CAR to buy any new stress. Competition is rising in retail, where ARCIL is investing in technology and its CAS platform.

qa_highlights.question: How do retail and SME acquisitions carry write-off risk, and what mix is being bought?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retail presence dates to 2008 and that the 3-4 year resolution cycle, plus in-house collections, limits write-off risk. H1 acquisitions were about INR700 crores corporate and about INR1,000 crores SME and retail. Write-offs occur about eight years after acquisition, and management expects only a very small amount to cross that threshold over the next three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why invest more in structured SR deals if they carry no upside income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said structured deals return the IRR mostly as regular fee income, while cash deals give larger upsides later in the holding period. Average investment across H1 acquisitions was 42%.

Entry into microfinance and expected growth in competition in retail and SME; the company said it is still testing the microfinance market.
Industry AUM has been flat per the Q&A; management attributed this to recoveries and write-offs by some ARCs rather than a structural issue.

544923|2026-09.headline: Veegaland Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28.7% YoY to INR106.34 crore and PAT rose 92% to INR15.99 crore, with PAT margin at 14.7%.

544940|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 standalone total income rose about 182% to INR52.37 crore, with PAT up about 395% to INR6.85 crore, as a carried-over order book was executed.
544940|2026-09.overview: Robokidz Eduventures reported H1 FY27 (half year to 30 Sep 2026), its first earnings call after listing on the BSE SME platform on 28 Sep 2026 (subscribed 834 times). Standalone total income rose to INR52.37 crore from INR18.55 crore, EBITDA to INR11.53 crore and PAT to INR6.85 crore. 545001|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 record quarter: revenue up 24.7% to INR373 crore, EBITDA up 36.6% to INR65 crore, with margin rising to 17.6%.
545001|2026-09.overview: Sahajanand Medical Technologies reported its first earnings call as a listed company, with Q2 FY27 setting record revenue, EBITDA and PAT. EBITDA grew faster than revenue on operating leverage in employee and other expenses, though gross margin fell about 170 bps in H1 on traded-product mix and input costs. Reported H1 PAT growth of 7.5% is depressed by a one-off INR8.7 crore tax credit in H1 FY26; excluding it, PAT grew about 39%. Management guided to 150-200 bps annual EBITDA margin expansion and mid-to-high teens constant-currency growth, while H1 free cash flow was slightly negative after capex.

+7.5% YoY; about +39% excluding INR8.7 crore one-off tax credit in H1 FY26
vs 76% a year ago (about -170 bps, of which ~150 bps mix)

financial_highlights.metric: H1 free cash flow (after capex and lease payments, before interest)

financial_highlights.change: close to 1x net debt/EBITDA; borrowings INR300 crore, cash and liquid investments INR114 crore
from 138 days in FY26 and about 144 days in FY25

segments.name: Vascular intervention
segments.commentary: 58% of H1 revenue, up 16% YoY; core business including stents, balloons and PTCA catheters.

segments.name: Structural heart
segments.commentary: Grew about 40% in Q2, with TAVI and occluders both up about 40%.

segments.name: Other (largely traded products, incl. IVUS in Europe)
segments.commentary: Fastest-growing category, up 52% in H1; trading now about 25-26% of revenue per analyst question, with management citing IVUS demand tailwind and EBITDA-accretive but gross-margin-dilutive economics.

segments.commentary: Grew 37% in H1 and is now the largest region at 40% of revenue.

segments.commentary: Grew a steady 23% in both quarters; 36% of revenue.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Growth accelerated from 6% in Q1 to 15% in Q2.

guidance_outlook: Constant-currency revenue growth in the mid-to-high teens; management said mid-teens is a conservative baseline for FY27 and FY28. Currency gains would be over and above this.
EBITDA margin expansion of 150-200 bps per year in FY27, FY28 and FY29, taking margin to about 20% by FY29 from 14.1% in FY26.
Capex of about INR70 crore in FY27 and about INR70 crore in FY28 (INR44 crore spent in H1 FY27), covering vertical integration, automation, maintenance at the Sachin plant and some capacity addition.
Effective tax rate expected at 32-35% for the next two to three years, due to higher-tax geographies (Spain, Brazil, Germany) and loss-making subsidiaries without deferred tax assets.
Working capital days expected to fall by about 15 days over three years, to roughly 100-110 days from about 128 days; inventory is the main lever, receivable days already at 75.
Hydra Elevate already CDSCO-approved; Hydra next-generation valve and AVDC 1.5/TAVI 2.0 launch expected in FY27, possibly as early as Q3 and no later than Q4; PTCA catheters targeted for FY28.
EU MDR: Supraflex Cruz certified; Pipit NC and SC completed audits; Hydra and Cocoon technical files submitted, ahead of the end-2027 transition deadline.
capex_capacity: FY27 and FY28 capex guidance of about INR70 crore per year; INR44 crore spent in H1 FY27. Mix: vertical integration, automation, maintenance at Sachin legacy plant, and a small capacity component.

Management said current capacity suffices for at least 1.5 years, with capex unlikely to rise meaningfully above INR70 crore for the next two to three years. It declined to give peak revenue capacity guidance.

DES utilisation H1 FY27: 79% at Surat and 20% at Telangana (from 64% at Telangana per the analyst's reference). Balloon utilisation: 72% at Surat and 57% at Telangana. New drug-coated balloon line at Surat at 40%.
Surat PTCA utilisation fell to 72% from 97% YoY; management attributed this to inventory optimisation, as previously produced stock was converted to revenue faster than expected.
Gross fixed asset turnover was about 7x before the Telangana plant; management expects it to rise as Telangana ramps up.

Hyderabad (Telangana) technical sterilisation capacity of 9,000 for TAVI in the RHP was not shown in the deck, which shows 3,000 commercial capacity at 60% utilisation. Management said ramp-up of TAVI or occluder capacity is not capex-intensive.
demand_pricing: India: DGHS notification on single-use devices is a tailwind, mainly for PTCA catheters (Pipit SC/NC); implants (stents, TAVI, occluders) cannot be reused. Management does not expect it to lift the 9-10% industry growth to 15-20%.

Europe: TAVI market share about 1.5% (not yet 2%) in low single digits; management expects faster traction once Hydra valve and AVDC are launched. Europe is the largest addressable region for structural heart.
Pricing: broadly stable across all product segments, negotiated hospital by hospital in India, with competitive landscape, product merit and commercial team capability as drivers.

Trading (other products) is rising on IVUS demand after reimbursement in developed markets about two years ago; management said it is gross-margin-dilutive but EBITDA-accretive because SG&A is shared.

International: TAVI not yet approved in Brazil; Australia launched and Canada approved recently. Stents present in more than 70 countries; countries with commercial presence fell to 70 in H1 from 77 in FY26 due to distributor bulk-buying timing, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 capex plan and how much has been spent?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR70 crore guided for each of FY27 and FY28, with about INR44 crore spent in H1 FY27, split across vertical integration, automation, Sachin plant maintenance and small capacity additions.

qa_highlights.question: Can gross margin improve via backward integration, and what is steady-state EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: No gross margin uplift quantified until processes are set up and cycles run; EBITDA margin guided up 150-200 bps a year, reaching about 20% by FY29, driven by European operating leverage with teams already in place.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the tax rate high?
qa_highlights.answer: ETR is around 35% because Spain, Brazil and Germany carry higher tax rates and some subsidiaries are loss-making without deferred tax assets; ETR expected at 32-35% for two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why do the RHP and deck show different TAVI capacity figures?
qa_highlights.answer: The RHP included Hyderabad technical sterilisation capacity, not yet commercialised, which the deck excludes; ramping TAVI or occluder capacity needs little capex.

qa_highlights.question: What is the constant-currency growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Mid-to-high teens, with mid-teens as the conservative baseline for both the current and next year; reported currency impact cannot be guided.

qa_highlights.answer: Around 15 days of further improvement over three years, to about 100-110 days from about 128 days, mainly from inventory reduction.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential on current capacity plus INR70 crore annual capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a peak revenue number, saying TAVI capacity at Hyderabad generates much more revenue per unit of capacity than stents and catheters, so no simple calculation is available.

qa_highlights.question: What is the market share in Europe for TAVI, and how will Europe's structural heart business grow?
qa_highlights.answer: TAVI market share is about 1.5% in Europe; Europe is the largest structural heart market and growth is expected to hold or accelerate with the new Hydra valve and AVDC launch.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of trading/others revenue (IVUS, OCT, thrombectomy) and the impact of the Boston Scientific acquisition of thrombectomy business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give product-level breakdown, citing its no-product-guidance policy; trading growth was attributed to IVUS reimbursement tailwind.

On the current capacity that we have, it will be sufficient for at least a year and a half.
Unfortunately, since we are not giving product -level guidances, I will refrain from doing that.
Some of the other major products that are in the pipeline are a little bit further out, somewhere around the two to three years out.

545004|2026-09.headline: Jio Platforms Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.4% YoY to ₹40,475 Cr, EBITDA up 16.6% to ₹21,879 Cr at a 54.1% margin.
545004|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the first quarter reported after listing; management reported 542.4 million customers, 36 million YoY net adds and 9.1 million adds in the quarter, with 5G base at 300 million. Consolidated revenue of ₹40,475 Cr grew 11.4% YoY, EBITDA of ₹21,879 Cr grew 16.6% and margin expanded about 250 bps YoY, with management saying ~78% of incremental revenue flowed to EBITDA. PAT rose 13.7% YoY to ₹8,387 Cr, and EBITDA less capex was ₹15,449 Cr for the quarter (up 52.5% YoY) and ₹32,130 Cr for H1. Management framed growth around four pillars (grow, deepen, convert, build) and pushed a 'digital gateway' model, while explicitly not using tariff hikes as the main ARPU lever. Net leverage was 0.11x at 30 September; the call also covered the IPO (about ₹30,188 Cr of issue proceeds, 24.5x oversubscribed) and international partnership plans.

financial_highlights.change: Net debt positive after IPO proceeds

segments.name: Connectivity (Jio consolidated connectivity entity)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹35,307 Cr, up 10.8% YoY; EBITDA ₹20,505 Cr, up 14.7% YoY, margin 58.1%.

segments.name: Standalone JPL (digital services and other)
segments.commentary: Standalone revenue up 23% YoY to ₹4,881 Cr, which management said captures the digital services monetisation not in the connectivity ARPU.

segments.commentary: Broadband homes reached 30 million, with ~7.3 million YoY net adds; roughly half of the base is fixed wireless access (FWA), and FWA drives most new additions.

segments.name: Mobility (5G)
segments.commentary: 5G customers reached 300 million (66 million YoY adds, 15 million QoQ); Jio holds 51% of wireless broadband subscribers and 60% of the 5G subscriber base.

guidance_outlook: Management said capex peak is behind it and capex for the next four to five years is not expected to exceed last year's level, so free cash flow should grow.
Dividends were not committed; management said growth is the priority and the first year as a listed company will be used to learn before deciding on payouts.
International: management targets 10 to 15 sizeable partners (not niche markets), using a managed-service, asset-light model rather than hardware or SaaS sales; no timing given.
Management said the Gemini offer's initial term is 18 months and it has not yet reached 12 months; no decision yet on charging after expiry.
Tariff increases: management said no decision yet and ARPU is not the only lever; timing will depend on market and macro conditions.
capex_capacity: 5G standalone investment is complete; management said capex for the next four to five years will not exceed FY27-level spend.
UBR (unlicensed broadband radio) home broadband stack has gone through four generations in about three years; management estimates a lead of at least 2.5 to 3 years over the nearest competitor.
Unlicensed UBR cost per user is about $3 against ARPU of about $6, per management, supporting the high-to-low ARPU market strategy.
Management said no incremental spectrum or capex is needed to convert the 4G base to 5G, per the call.
Radisys (already owned) is the existing channel for technology supply to operators, cited as the model for partnerships without direct competition.
demand_pricing: Management sees 340 million new mobility users (240 million from 2G users with other operators, ~100 million from demographic additions over five years).
Fixed broadband penetration is ~20% of ~330 million homes (~64 million connected); management targets ~46% by FY2031 and sees 150 million as a potential fixed broadband opportunity.
Digital economy target of $1.4 trillion cited; 80 million small merchants and 350,000 leased lines are cited as enterprise opportunities.
Digital services: Gemini voice AI usage rose from 2 minutes to over 7 minutes; home subscribers pay about 15% more for 13 OTT apps bundled, per management.
Competition: management said Jio's FWA base is 2x the nearest operator and it expects 5G adds to be driven by 4G-to-5G migration and share gains from other operators.

qa_highlights.question: Go-to-market for digital services, scale expected over 2-3 years, and international partnership timing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said digital revenue will come from enterprise, home and mobility; partnership talks are two-way, with equal engagement on UBR and full OSS/BSS stack; no timing was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why there is no converged single bill for connectivity and digital services.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is focusing on converged go-to-market and one bill, but said that story is still to play out.

qa_highlights.question: Free cash flow, dividends and capex intensity given the asset-light model.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said capex has peaked and will not exceed last year's level for four to five years; management said growth is the priority and dividends will be considered after the first listed year.

qa_highlights.question: Tariff hikes and ARPU, given about 2.5 years since last hike.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tariffs depend on several factors and it will decide at the right time; ARPU rose 3.5% YoY organically, and the focus is digital services realisations.

qa_highlights.question: Conflict of interest in international partnerships, given Jio's own connectivity business.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not give technology to domestic players, will avoid competing with partners, and the Radisys model is the reference for partnerships.

qa_highlights.question: AI monetisation (token charges) and Gemini pricing after free period.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Gemini deal runs 18 months, is not near expiry, and that AI will be offered via the telecom harness to the full base; no token charging decided.

qa_highlights.question: Starlink and satellite competition in India and the US.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said satellite direct-to-device capacity is far lower than terrestrial (about 20 kbps per sq km), that Jio covers 99% of India's homes, and that it plans its own LEO system as a complement.

qa_highlights.question: Financial metrics that management wants to hit over five to seven years.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a single number and said it will track market share, deployment, and ARPU uplift; it cited FY26 EBITDA above $8 billion.

International strategy has zero customers and zero revenue; partnerships are not yet signed and no timing was given.
Competition from satellite (Starlink) and other FWA players; management claims a 2.5 to 3 year technology lead, which is not independently verified.
Watch next quarter for: any tariff move, first international partner announcement, converged billing rollout, and dividend policy.

545005|2026-09.headline: Paras Healthcare Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23% to INR 511 crore and operating EBITDA 47% to INR 120 crore, margin 23.5%.
545005|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's first earnings call after its listing on 28 October 2026. Revenue from operations grew 23% YoY to INR 511 crore, operating EBITDA rose 47% to INR 120 crore, and PAT reached INR 40.3 crore versus INR 12.4 crore a year earlier. Growth came from the mature cluster (revenue up 8.5%), emerging hospitals (up 27%) and new hospitals Srinagar and Kanpur (revenue up 2.4x), which turned EBITDA-positive in Q2. Working capital absorbed INR 172 crore in H1, lifting receivables to INR 518 crore and DSO to about 92 days, while Udaipur was softer due to a suspended Rajasthan state government scheme.

segments.name: Mature hospitals (Gurgaon, Patna, Panchkula, Darbhanga)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue up 8.5% and H1 revenue up 9.1%; Q2 operating EBITDA margin 29.6% (+360 bps), H1 28.9%; H1 occupancy 76.5%.

segments.name: Emerging hospitals (Ranchi, Udaipur)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue up 27.2%, H1 up 43.2%; H1 EBITDA margin 18.3% vs 12.4%; H1 occupancy 68.6% vs 49.1%. Ranchi delivered 25.8% EBITDA margin in Q2; Udaipur was softer.

segments.name: New hospitals (Srinagar, Kanpur)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 139% in Q2 and 147% in H1; operating EBITDA turned from negative INR 13 crore in FY26 to INR 15.8 crore in Q2 and above INR 25 crore in H1; H1 margin 18.7%; H1 occupancy 68.4% vs 27.8%.

About 200-250 beds to be operationalised in Kanpur (remaining half of 435-bed capacity) and Ranchi, taking operational beds from about 1,500 to about 1,800, by end of FY27.
Emerging hospitals expected to move to mature cohort over 4-7 years, then reach low-to-mid 20s margins before mid-to-high 20s when mature.
Gurgaon Golf Course Extension (300 beds) and Ludhiana (500 beds, next year) are the next capacity additions; 800 beds coming on stream over the next 12-18 months to 20-24 months.
Remaining INR 125 crore of IPO proceeds to be used for debt repayment, lowering interest cost.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about INR 90 crore across units, including payments for Gurgaon 2 (Golf Course Extension).
Kanpur has 435 bed capacity; roughly half opened, two wings yet to open by end of FY27.
Ludhiana 500-bed expansion expected next year; Gurgaon 2 adds 300 beds.
New and upcoming facilities are to remain asset-light; M&A, greenfield, brownfield and O&M models are open but current focus is on the two projects.
Quaternary programmes: liver transplant (Gurgaon, extended to Panchkula and Patna), kidney and bone marrow transplant; robotic surgery in Gurgaon, Patna, Panchkula, Ranchi and Udaipur (ortho).
demand_pricing: Group occupancy Q2 FY27 76.3% vs 62.5% YoY; H1 73% vs 59%; occupied bed days up 23.9% to 201,000.
Inpatient volumes up 27.3% and outpatient volumes up 20.4% in H1 YoY.
ARPOB H1 FY27 INR 48,900 vs INR 48,400; ALOS 2.8 days vs 2.9 days.
H1 payor mix: 32% cash/self-pay, 24% insurance, 44% government schemes and PSUs.

Rajasthan state government scheme temporarily suspended across multiple Rajasthan hospitals, hurting Udaipur; management says Udaipur cash and insurance business grew in absolute terms and recovered 30-40% of lost state scheme business.
Kanpur EBITDA margin improved from -22.8% to 15.6%; Kanpur occupancy 78.4% in H1 FY27 vs 22.7% in H1 FY26. Srinagar occupancy 60.4% in H1.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Udaipur soft this quarter and could its revenue fall YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet Aggarwal said the Rajasthan state government scheme was under review and temporarily suspended across multiple hospitals; Udaipur's cash and insurance business grew, recovering 30-40% of lost state-scheme business. Management is working to reduce government-scheme dependence.

qa_highlights.question: Why is receivables build-up (cash flow negative INR 172 crore working capital) so large year-on-year?
qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Bidani attributed it to 25% business growth, a higher share of empanelments in new hospitals, and lumpy payments from certain payor groups; DSO rose from about 79 days (March) to 92 days (September). Trade receivables rose from INR 87.5 crore to INR 124 crore YoY per the analyst; management said it expects it to settle as payor mix improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 50 crore item in other financial assets in operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Bidani said it is a long-term fixed deposit with regular bankers, created from the INR 80 crore equity infusion in April 2025 and classified as non-current under accounting standards.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin for mature hospitals and how will margins evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Bidani said new hospitals move from negative to mid-to-high teens margins, then emerging, then mature (currently mid-to-high 20s blended). Long-term steady-state blended margin envisaged in the mid-20s; not a guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is there ALOS and seasonality sustainability into Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet Aggarwal said ALOS has consistently been 2.8-3.0 days and expected to continue; case mix, daycare and robotic surgery drive it. Seasonality reflects North and East India locations; occupancy to be supported by existing capacity and bed additions.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company stay asset-light and is acquisition a low priority?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Nagar said Gurgaon and Ludhiana remain asset-light; M&A, greenfield, brownfield and PPP are open, but current focus is delivering the two projects over the next two years.

risks_watch: Receivables rose from INR 350 crore (March 2026) to INR 518 crore (September 2026) and DSO to about 92 days; H1 OCF only INR 68 crore against PAT of INR 90 crore.
Rajasthan state scheme suspension affecting Udaipur; revenue may decline YoY there until scheme resumes.
Dependence on government and PSU schemes at 44% of H1 payor mix.
Ramp-up of Kanpur (about half of 435 beds still unopened) and Ranchi beds by year-end; Srinagar occupancy at 60.4%.
Execution of Gurgaon Golf Course Extension and Ludhiana (800 beds) and doctor recruitment for specialty and quaternary programmes; talent shortage cited in Darbhanga.
No formal guidance; watch next quarter's disclosures on DSO, net debt and interest cost savings.
545005|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and margins, with candour on weak spots: management openly flagged Udaipur's softness and working-capital build-up, but gave no numeric guidance, deferring to a long-term margin model framed as not guidance.
key_quotes: Margin expanded by 390 basis points to 23.5%.
Of the INR 500 crores of fresh issue, INR 375 crores has already gone to repay and prepay borrowings.
Udaipur was softer, and of course, the teams will talk about it, our operations will talk about it.
There is no guidance as such which we are sharing.

vs INR 12.4 crore YoY; EPS INR 4
+58% YoY vs INR 142 crore; operating margin 23% vs 18.1%

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Kanpur ~200-250 beds and Ranchi beds due by end FY27 (operational beds ~1,500 to ~1,800), and Gurgaon Golf Course Extension (300 beds) is under construction with capex of about INR 90 crore in H1 FY27.

rows.why: Srinagar and Kanpur turned from negative INR 13 crore EBITDA in FY26 to INR 15.8 crore in Q2 FY27, with H1 margin 18.7% and occupancy 68.4% vs 27.8%.

tone.note: Management was confident on occupancy, ARPOB stability, margin expansion and bed additions, and candid on Udaipur's softness and the working-capital build-up; analysts pushed on receivables, DSO, the INR 50 crore fixed deposit item in operating cash flow and the sustainability of margins.

545008|2026-09.headline: EAAA India Alternatives H1 FY27: fee-paying AUM up 23% three-year CAGR to Rs 49,164 crore; H1 PAT Rs 169 crore, up 35% YoY.
545008|2026-09.overview: First earnings call after the company's listing earlier in the month, covering the half year ended 30 September 2026. Management said fee-paying AUM reached Rs 49,164 crore, with a 23% three-year rolling CAGR and 28% one-year growth. Total income was Rs 616 crore (up 35% YoY) and PAT Rs 169 crore (up 35% YoY), with management and advisory fees at Rs 333 crore (up 24%). Management reiterated medium-to-long-term targets of 20-30% growth in fee-paying AUM and PAT, a 30% ROE aspiration and about 50% payout. Transcript quality is poor in places, so some figures and terms may be garbled.

financial_highlights.change: 23% three-year CAGR; 28% one-year growth from about Rs 38,500 crore

financial_highlights.value: Rs 7 per share (140% of face value)

financial_highlights.change: non-fee-paying / dry powder about Rs 20,000-25,000 crore

segments.name: Income and yield strategies (credit, real assets)
segments.commentary: About 49% of AUM from institutional LPs and 51% from HNI, UHNI and family offices; 77% of AUM from repeat clients and 5,750+ unique client relationships. Real-asset holdings include about 5.6 million sq ft of completed office, about 7,700 km of roads, 1.73 GW solar and about 1,800 circuit km of transmission.

segments.name: Fundraising and deployment
segments.commentary: About Rs 31,000 crore raised over FY26 and H1 FY27, of which about Rs 11,000 crore in listed InvIT strategies and about Rs 20,000 crore in fund strategies. Won TOT-19 road bundle under the National Monetisation Plan at Rs 2,259 crore (about 600 lane-km, Tamil Nadu), and acquired a 95%-occupied Grade A office park in Pune (about 1 million sq ft).

segments.name: Realisations
segments.commentary: Collected upwards of Rs 6,300 crore across strategies in H1. Fully exited Infrastructure Fund I, which generated a 19.3% gross return; the exit pulled forward distribution-cost amortisation into Q1.

guidance_outlook: Target 20-30% growth in fee-paying AUM and PAT over the medium to long term.
Aspire to PAT yield of 65-70 bps on fee-paying AUM.
VAR-related earnings expected at 25-30% of overall PAT; VAR earnings now spread across seven funds and five strategies.
Aim for 30% ROE and distribute around 50% of annual earnings on a long-term basis.

Fundraising ongoing over the next few quarters for Special Situations, Infrastructure Yield, second-vintage Commercial Real Estate and Private Equity (new PE fund expected to be nearly 3x the previous fund).
capex_capacity: Owned and operated assets include about 5.6 million sq ft of completed office space, about 7,700 km of roads, 1.73 GW of solar and about 1,800 circuit km of transmission lines.
TOT-19 road bundle (Rs 2,259 crore) acquired under the National Monetisation Plan.
Pune office park (about 1 million sq ft, 95% occupied) added to the commercial office strategy.
Private equity platform in its second vintage; three portfolio companies already listed, with Brentomojo the latest.
demand_pricing: Management says the Indian alternatives industry is about 4% of GDP versus about 30% in North America, and that yield and income strategies will grow from about 33% to about 42% of the industry.
Distribution cost averages about 30 bps; roughly 60 bps on the distributed portion (50:50 mix), amortised over 6-7 years to about 3.5-4% of distributed AUM.
No revenue-sharing with distributors, per management.
Management said net-of-distribution yield to clients is the focus; institutional clients sometimes pay full fee with no distribution cost.

qa_highlights.question: How does the visibility of variable returns (carry) in income and yield strategies compare with PE or VC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hurdle returns on the six-to-eight-year closed-end funds do not compound because income strategies pay annual cash flows, and returns are non-equity correlated, so carry visibility is fairly high, especially for own-and-operate assets with contracted cash flows.

qa_highlights.question: What is the distribution mix (direct vs external distributors) and is there distributor concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the HNI, UHNI and family-office segments (about 49% of AUM per the answer) are distributor-led, while institutions are direct. No top-three or top-five distributor concentration figure was given in the answer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total commitment and dry powder figure as of 30 September?
qa_highlights.answer: Total AUM is about Rs 95,000 crore; the non-fee-paying portion (dry powder that converts into fee-paying AUM as deployed) is about Rs 20,000-25,000 crore. Management said the finance team would provide the breakup.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Q1 distribution expense booked in one go?
qa_highlights.answer: Infrastructure Fund I was exited early, before its scheduled end, so the remaining forward-period distribution cost was amortised into Q1 in full.

qa_highlights.question: Do real assets and credit differ in unit economics and distribution cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said real assets are lower-beta but the fund-level unit economics are aimed to be similar across strategies, with focus on net yield after distribution cost; the Infrastructure Fund I gross return of 19.3% was cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management fee growth (24%) below fee-paying AUM growth (about 28% one-year)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a clear reconciling explanation; it pointed to the fee-paying AUM CAGR as the focus metric and referred to the Q1 Infrastructure Fund I exit affecting the mix.

risks_watch: Q1 included a one-time distribution-cost amortisation from the early exit of Infrastructure Fund I; watch for normalisation of Q2 and H2 fee and PAT run-rate.
Management fee growth (24%) lagging fee-paying AUM growth; monitor fee-yield trend.
Dry powder of about Rs 20,000-25,000 crore must be deployed to convert into fee-paying AUM; deployment pace matters for the 20-30% growth target.
Distribution dependence: about half of AUM comes from HNI, UHNI and family-office channels with distribution costs of about 60 bps on that portion.
Carry and VAR earnings timing is lumpy, and the company targets only 25-30% of PAT from VAR.
Transcript quality is poor; several figures and names should be verified against the investor presentation and filings.
545008|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and growth-focused on fundraising, deployment and the long-term alternatives thesis. Management was more guarded on distributor mix and unit economics, deferring detailed breakups to follow-up materials.
key_quotes: It has been our motto capabilities before capital and we have our in-house operating platform called Secura
We have always focused on our fee paying AUM on a three-year CAGR basis.
We have decided to keep this capability in house even though in the short term it might look costlier

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: PAT yield on fee-paying AUM is about 0.72% in H1 (0.71% in Q2) against an aspirational 65-70 bps target, but Q1 carried a one-time distribution-cost amortisation from the early Infrastructure Fund I exit and cost-to-income is steady at 64-65%, so no clear expansion is signalled.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Pune office park (about 1 million sq ft, 95% occupied) and TOT-19 road bundle (Rs 2,259 crore, about 600 lane-km) are added, and Rs 20,000-25,000 crore of dry powder is to be deployed, but no new capacity timeline was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Fee-paying AUM reached Rs 49,164 crore, up 28% one-year, against a 20-30% medium-to-long-term growth target, backed by about Rs 31,000 crore raised in FY26 and H1 FY27 and ongoing fundraising.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the platform is asset-light fund management and the TOT-19 and Pune acquisitions are deal-driven rather than capex-driven.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 PAT rose 35% YoY and total income 35%, and management reiterated 20-30% growth targets rather than raising them, so an upgrade is conditional on fundraising and deployment.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management fee growth (24%) lags fee-paying AUM growth (28%), dry powder of Rs 20,000-25,000 crore must be deployed, and carry income is lumpy with VAR capped at 25-30% of PAT.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Fundraising is ongoing for Special Situations, Infrastructure Yield, second-vintage Commercial Real Estate and a new PE fund expected to be nearly 3x the previous fund.

rows.label: Dry powder deployment into fee-paying AUM
rows.why: Non-fee-paying AUM of about Rs 20,000-25,000 crore converts to fee-paying AUM as deployed, against total AUM of about Rs 95,000 crore, supporting the 20-30% growth target.

rows.label: Distribution cost normalisation after Infrastructure Fund I exit
rows.why: The Q1 exit pulled forward the remaining distribution-cost amortisation, so Q2 PAT of Rs 88 crore (up 9% QoQ) reflects a lower run-rate charge and should normalise thereafter.

rows.label: Private equity fund vintage 2 nearly 3x prior fund
rows.why: Management expects the new PE fund to be nearly 3x the previous fund, but fundraising timing was not given and the outcome depends on investor demand.

tone.note: Management was confident on fundraising, deployment and the 20-30% growth thesis, but guarded on distributor mix and unit economics; analysts probed why management fee growth (24%) lags AUM growth (28%) and the one-time Q1 distribution-cost charge.

570004|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 4% to INR1,800 crore and EBITDA about 7%, but a March raw-material shock cost an estimated INR200-250 crore of sales.
570004|2026-03.overview: Management said Q4 consolidated revenue was about INR1,800 crore versus about INR1,750 crore a year earlier, with Hi-Tech up about 8% and plastics down slightly. Consolidated EBITDA grew about 7% and margin rose to 13.2% from 12.8%, with Hi-Tech margin at 19.8% versus 17.5%. For FY26, revenue grew about 11% and Hi-Tech grew over 20%, while plastics grew only 2.4%. Reported PAT was negative at about INR40 crore due to one-time deferred tax unwinding, a Labour Code charge and non-cash NCD unwinding; management cited adjusted PAT of about INR133 crore. Management says debt repayments due in September and March FY27 are to be met from internal accruals and government receivables, with refinancing and equity as backups.

segments.name: Hi-Tech (drip irrigation, tissue culture, solar agri pumps)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up about 8% and EBITDA up about 22%, margin 19.8%. FY26 revenue grew more than 20%. Domestic business grew about 12% and retail about 13%, below the company's 15%-plus target because of March sales loss.

segments.name: Plastics (piping, plastic sheets)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue slightly down, EBITDA up 3.3%, margin 10.2% versus 9.7%. FY26 revenue grew only 2.4% and EBITDA declined. Overseas plastic sheet business is doing reasonably well.

segments.name: Agro Processing / Food
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew about 6% but EBITDA declined. FY26 revenue crossed INR2,000 crore, up 9%, with EBITDA up about 9%. UK food revenue rose from GBP 60 million to GBP 68 million, with cost headwinds. Beverage bottling lines (juice and CSD) started in Q4; about INR27-28 crore revenue was booked by end-March.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 to be better than FY26 on revenue, margins, cash flow and balance sheet, though it called FY27 an uncertain year.
Company plans to be PAT positive (reported) in FY27, with positive EPS targeted from next year.

Management expects standalone operating cash flow to rise from about INR350 crore to INR750-800 crore in FY27, with about INR450 crore of government receivables expected to come down and about INR150 crore of government benefits.
Management expects the second half of Q4 to be better than the first half and July onwards to be better than before, if there is no new price shock.
Management said it would not give numerical guidance because of uncertainty, but said FY28 onwards will be focused on growth funded by internal accruals.
Food business expected to improve in FY27 with the end of UK and US cost and market headwinds, duty-free onion imports under India-USDA rules, and beverage expansion.
capex_capacity: Two beverage bottling lines (one juice, one CSD) started in Q4; about INR140 crore invested over December and March quarters, with no incremental working capital needed per management.
Discussions ongoing for 3 additional beverage lines in FY27, with investment decision expected soon.
Tomato processing plant with a Japanese collaborator expected to start around January 2027, ahead of the tomato season.
Alwar plant near Delhi in Rajasthan is being expanded to grow in North India.
Land sale in Tamil Nadu under MoU, expected to close in the next one to two months, per management.
demand_pricing: Raw material shock: PVC and polyethylene prices rose sharply between 20 February and 25 March 2026, with polymer prices more than 50% higher at peak (polyethylene about 60%) within about 20 days.
By late April-early May, PVC had fallen to about 10% above February levels, while HDPE/LLDPE remained about 40% higher; PVC demand has returned.
Farmers postponed purchases in March and April due to price uncertainty and lower prices for farm produce as exports fell.
Management attributes an INR200-250 crore shortfall in Q4 revenue to the March pricing shock; standalone Q4 revenue was about INR1,000 crore versus a potential INR1,250 crore-plus.

Drip irrigation sales FY26: Maharashtra about INR700 crore, South about INR400 crore, West about INR250 crore, North about INR88 crore (up from INR75 crore), East about INR107 crore (up from INR60 crore).

qa_highlights.question: How will the company service its debt given weak standalone cash flow, and what restructuring or fundraise is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said standalone operating cash flow should rise from about INR350 crore to INR750-800 crore, with about INR150 crore of government benefits also available. Backup options include refinancing and equity, with more clarity expected by July. Management said a smaller amount is due in September and most in March FY27, and that about 98% of old interest-bearing term debt was repaid by March.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Tamil Nadu asset sale close to closing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an MoU is signed for the Tamil Nadu land and it should close over the next couple of weeks to a month, after recent state elections.

qa_highlights.question: When will PAT turn positive, and what is the adjusted PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the FY27 plan is reported PAT positive. Reported FY26 PAT was minus INR40 crore due to one-time items and non-cash NCD unwinding; adjusted PAT was about INR133 crore versus INR97 crore earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What are the bottling plant and UK food business progress and investment?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR140 crore has been invested in bottling over two quarters; first line is operating and about INR27-28 crore revenue was booked by end-March. UK food revenue grew to GBP 68 million from GBP 60 million, with cost headwinds expected to ease in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an IPO plan for the food division?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is some distance away because of market conditions, and is unlikely in the first half of FY27, subject to merchant banker advice.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 revenue short of expectations (about INR200-250 crore), and by segment where?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the shortfall entirely to the March pricing shock and lost farmer demand. It said standalone EBITDA would have been about INR25 crore higher had the sales been realised, and that margins were held.

risks_watch: Debt repayments due in September and a larger amount in March FY27 depend on collection of government and project receivables, and refinancing or equity is the backup.
Polymer prices (HDPE/LLDPE still about 40% higher) and the risk of another price shock affecting Q1 and H1 FY27 demand.
Reported PAT remains negative; the FY27 PAT-positive target depends on cash-based earnings and non-cash items.
Exports fell about 10% in FY26 to INR455 crore; tariffs, shipping constraints and geopolitical risk remain.
UK and US food business cost and market headwinds, and the timing of new beverage lines and tomato plant start.
570004|2026-03.management_tone: Management was confident on debt servicing and the FY27 outlook but cautious on near-term demand, repeatedly citing uncertainty. It gave few numbers on Q1 FY27 and refused to give detailed guidance, and it deflected questions on partners and on the food IPO.
key_quotes: And since then, if I talk about late April, early May, PVC prices have come down because part of PVC gets supplied from China, which is coal-based, and that comes at a lower cost.
So the entire reduction, about INR200 crores, INR250 crores is linked to this pricing shock in March.
And we feel that company would be able to generate adequate internal accruals to be able to take care of that matter.
For FY '27, right, our plan right now is to be PAT positive.

570004|2026-06.headline: Jain Irrigation Q1 FY27 revenue fell ~2.5% to about Rs 1,500 crore, EBITDA margin dropped ~2 pts, and adjusted PAT was about Rs 3 crore versus Rs 30 crore a year ago.
570004|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was about Rs 1,500 crore, down roughly 2.5% YoY, with Hi-Tech degrowing, plastics flat and Agro-Processing growing on beverages and overseas sales. EBITDA fell on lower standalone India fixed-cost absorption, weaker Hi-Tech volumes and negative forex, while plastics margin improved. Management said April was weak but May, June and July improved, and it expects a stronger second half. Rs 164 crore of EBITDA was converted to cash at about 78%, and net working capital days fell to 183 from 210 a year ago. Rs 680-690 crore of NCDs fall due in September (about Rs 230 crore) and March; management says these will be met from internal cash flow with refinancing and other options in progress.

segments.commentary: Revenue down about 22% YoY; retail down 17% (MIS down 16% to Rs 368 crore, tissue culture down 10%) and project down 63%. Margin fell from 16.6% to 14.4%; management guides to double-digit growth for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much legacy government receivable will be collected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of about Rs 422 crore for FY27, with Rs 60 crore received in Q1 and at least Rs 380 crore expected in the remaining nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any risk of write-offs on project receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no material write-offs are expected; provisions were made in earlier review and the remaining good receivables will be collected.

qa_highlights.question: Why are standalone working capital requirements higher than peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to long-tail legacy project receivables and state-government orders on behalf of farmers, which are paid in six months to one year. Expects improvement from FY28 once project receivables clear.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the delay in the food business IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Market valuations fell over the past year, so merchant bankers advised waiting; the total issue, including PE exit and primary funds, was expected at about Rs 1,000 crore. Management expects action from September if markets improve.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Hi-Tech margin down and what is the full-year view?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin fell to 14.4% from 16.6% on lower volumes. Management said a full-year standalone margin of about 14% and consolidated 12-13% is maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the receivables are over 180 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs 1,100 crore is above 180 days (about Rs 300 crore of farmer-order receivables plus Rs 800-900 crore of government receivables), roughly 55% of the Rs 1,975 crore net receivables.

risks_watch: Debt service: about Rs 230 crore of NCDs due in September; refinancing and asset monetisation timelines remain unconfirmed.
Recovery of Rs 380 crore of legacy government receivables in nine months; about 55% of net receivables (about Rs 1,100 crore) are above 180 days.
Polymer price volatility and oil/geopolitical risk could delay customer purchases.
Monsoon progress in August-September, which management says is critical for H2 volumes.
Food business IPO and PE exit timing with no confirmed date; Tamil Nadu land sale repeatedly delayed.
Whether the H2 margin catch-up materialises; Q1 adjusted PAT was about Rs 3 crore.
key_quotes: So, all in all, reduction in EBITDA temporarily in this quarter, but we believe we should be able to catch up in the second half of the current fiscal year to cover what is lost.
And we are very confident on honoring the debt obli gation, we don't see that as an issue.
So, there is no pushback. I think because the payme nts are only due in September, right, end of September.
So, I think what we have not been able to do in the 1st Quarter, and I think 2nd Quarter i s always mute, but you should see improvement in the second half of the year.

570004|2026-09.headline: Jain Irrigation Q2 FY27 revenue rose over 10% to about INR 1,576 crore, EBITDA INR 207 crore, working capital cycle cut to 179 days.
570004|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew more than 10% to about INR 1,576 crore and EBITDA rose YoY to about INR 207 crore, though margin eased to 13.2% from 13.9%. Adjusted PAT after the NCD wind-down adjustment was about INR 40 crore. Cash conversion was strong, with about INR 206 crore of EBITDA converted to cash, which funded INR 230 crore of NCD repayments. Management said the drought in west and south India and high polymer prices weigh on the next six months, and guided only to flattish H2 volume.

financial_highlights.value: about INR 207 crore (quoted as INR 208 crore later)

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (Q2 FY27, after NCD wind-down adjustment)

financial_highlights.change: down from 183 days in Q1 and 205 days at end Sep 2025

segments.name: Hi-Tech MI (drip and tissue culture)
segments.commentary: Maintained high-teens growth and about 18.8% margin in Q2; domestic retail grew about 18%. Management targets 18%-19% margin medium term.

segments.name: Piping
segments.commentary: Down 25%-30% in Q1, roughly flat YoY in Q2 (revenue neutral). Management expects 8%-10% growth for full FY27, driven by non-agri applications such as large diameter pipes.

segments.name: Agro-processing (food)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR 560 crore in the quarter, up about 8.4%; margin around 12%. Phase two beverage capex of about INR 100 crore is planned for March-June 2027 quarter.

segments.name: Plastics (domestic and overseas)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 17% in Q2; margin about 9%. Medium-term target is about 12%.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 revenue expected at least flattish YoY; growth above last year depends on January visibility and easing polymer prices.
Net reduction in government-linked receivables of at least INR 300 crore by March 2027, from about INR 1,200 crore (project about INR 800 crore plus MIP about INR 400 crore).
Expected incentive receipt of about INR 100 crore (Maharashtra) and land monetisation of INR 100-150 crore by March 2027.
Project business expected to reach zero in FY28; most remaining project work and recovery expected within the next 12 months.
Interest saving of about INR 20 crore per year in FY28 after repayment of the 0% NCDs.
Working capital cycle reduction expected over the next 12 months; balance sheet to look much better in FY28.
Margin uplift of 1%-2% expected when polymer prices fall and capacity utilisation improves; no negative pricing impact expected from falling input costs.
capex_capacity: Tomato JV (food): about INR 30-40 crore required in March 2027 quarter, subject to completing asset acquisition by December 2026.
Beverage phase two: about INR 100 crore investment, mostly March-June 2027 quarter; work has started.
Biochar: major growth capex deferred to FY28; current year is proof of concept, with carbon credits and field trials ongoing.
Annual India interest cost about INR 50 crore per quarter (unchanged after NCD repayment, apart from about INR 20 crore annual saving from unwinding charges).
demand_pricing: Drought: management called it the worst monsoon in about 35 years nationally and more than 50 years in Maharashtra; west and south (80%-85% of business) most affected. Kharif hit, Rabi likely hit.
Polymer prices elevated due to West Asia conflict; farmers postponing purchases, with possible demand booster if prices ease between December and March.
Piping rural demand weak as resin costs are high; competitors sell more to urban and plumbing markets.
Coffee tissue culture orders received from the Coffee Board; coffee still small. Banana is the largest tissue culture crop, followed by pomegranate.
Solar water pump demand continuing; food processing and beverage demand picking up globally.
Business let go in H1 FY27: about INR 200-250 crore total (about INR 100 crore micro-irrigation in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu; about INR 150 crore solar pump), due to slow collections.

qa_highlights.question: Why is piping not growing while peers grow, and will it turn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Jain sells almost entirely into rural agriculture while competitors sell into urban plumbing and drainage. Piping was down 25%-30% in Q1 and revenue neutral in Q2; full-year growth of 8%-10% is expected.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the about INR 1,850 crore receivables will be collected by March, and how much is government-linked?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 800 crore is project-linked and about INR 400 crore MIP (government subsidy), totalling about INR 1,200 crore. Net reduction of at least INR 300 crore expected by March, which management said is enough for March obligations.

qa_highlights.question: What is the project revenue for FY27 and H1?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 project revenue about INR 33 crore; H2 expected INR 60-70 crore, mostly from the Pune water supply project. Management does not expect write-offs as provisions were already made.

qa_highlights.question: How much business was let go in H1 due to liquidity?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 200-250 crore: about INR 100 crore of micro-irrigation in southern states with slow payments and about INR 150 crore of solar pump business.

qa_highlights.question: How will H2 compare with last year, and what affects it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects at least flattish H2 given drought; upside depends on polymer prices easing and a December-March demand recovery, to be clarified in January.

qa_highlights.question: What will interest savings be in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 20 crore per year, mainly from the 0% NCDs being repaid; the main interest cost of about INR 50 crore per quarter is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold when polymer prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing uses average inventory cost, so no negative margin impact is expected on falling prices; fixed-cost absorption could add 1%-2% margin.

risks_watch: Drought in west and south India (80%-85% of business) could hit Rabi demand and cut utilisation.
Polymer price volatility and supply tied to West Asia conflict; any reversal could cut or delay farmer purchases.
Execution of about INR 800 crore project and MIP receivables and the INR 300 crore net reduction target by March 2027.
Repayment of about INR 450-500 crore NCD obligations due by March 2027; incentive and land monetisation (about INR 200-250 crore combined) timing.
Tomato JV asset acquisition closing by December 2026; growth capex timing for beverage phase two.

590003|2026-03.headline: KVB posted record FY26 net profit of INR2,500 crores (+29%) and Q4 NIM of 4.25%, but guides FY27 NIM down to 3.75-3.8% and ROA to 1.7-1.8%.
590003|2026-03.overview: Karur Vysya Bank reported record quarterly net profit of INR725 crores and full-year profit of INR2,500 crores (+29%), with full-year NIM of 3.97% above guidance. Total business grew 15% to INR2,14,420 crores, with advances up 17% to INR98,754 crores and deposits up 13% to INR1,15,666 crores, though advances growth moderated in Q4 by conscious choice. Management flagged a shift toward preserving relationships over margins: FY27 credit growth is guided at 1-2% above industry, NIM at 3.75-3.8%, and ROA at 1.7-1.8%. Asset quality stayed stable with GNPA at 0.75% and a one-time INR163 crore prudential provision taken against geopolitically exposed sectors.

financial_highlights.change: Highest quarterly profit in bank history
Includes INR163 crore one-time prudential provision

financial_highlights.value: INR187 crores (Q4); INR744 crores (FY26, 0.75% of loans)
financial_highlights.change: FY26 includes ~INR200 crore Q2 chunky slippages
Cost of deposits down 13 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.value: INR679 crores (FY26) excluding INR139 crore interest recovery

segments.name: Retail advances
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 25% YoY and 3% QoQ, driven by mortgages (+56% YoY) and jewel loans (+61% YoY). Housing loans grew only 2%, and BNPL book stands at INR798 crores after a partner management change.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri book grew 19% YoY (5% QoQ) per the call, with agri jewel loans at 91% of agri and LTV of 55.59%; management also cites 5% growth for the year, which is inconsistent with the 19% figure.

segments.name: Commercial and corporate
segments.commentary: Commercial book grew 11.56% YoY but was flat in Q4; corporate grew 12% YoY, or 20% including credit substitutes (incremental INR969 crores). Growth focused on CRE, capital markets and EPC contractors.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: CASA grew 12%, adding INR3,290 crores vs INR677 crores last year; savings deposits added INR2,505 crores. Bulk deposits grew 9% YoY vs 44% prior year, and CDs of INR1,773 crores were reduced in March.

guidance_outlook: FY27 credit growth guided at 1-2% above industry growth, versus 18% achieved in FY26 (RAM and corporate mix 18-20%, with ~5% flex).
FY27 NIM guided at 3.75-3.8% (management also cited 3.7-3.8% on the call), with exit-Q4 NIM above 4%; drop expected from retail term deposit repricing from April 2026 and lower advance yields.
FY27 ROA guided at 1.7-1.8%; credit cost guided at below 1%.
GNPA below 1.5%, net NPA below 1%, slippages below 1% of the asset book, cost-to-income below 50%, LCR maintained at 115-120%.

Branch expansion of 50 branches in FY27 (38 regular, 7 lite, 5 to be shortlisted), front-loaded into H1. Investment yield enhancement of 15-20 bps via HTM rebalancing; duration to be kept around 4-4.5 years over the medium term.

Management sees no need to raise capital in FY27; profit ploughback to fund growth. Dividend declared at 130%, subject to shareholder approval, with the payout on a larger base after the 1:5 bonus issued last year.
capex_capacity: Plan to open 50 branches in FY27: 38 regular, 7 lite, and 5 yet to be shortlisted; front-loading into H1 to capture benefit in Q2.
Management says capital is not a constraint: CRAR at 18.76% with Tier 1 dominant and RWA-to-total-assets at 55-58%, with room to take it up to around 65% over time.
Loan-against-mutual-fund IT integration is at final stage, expected launch in H1 FY27; premium credit cards planned in FY27.
Digital: 98% of transactions digital; DLite app rated 4.8 on Google Play and 4.6 on Apple App Store, with 2.5 million monthly active users.
demand_pricing: Retail term deposit rates raised in April 2026; new products at 7.2%, with blended incremental cost seen at 7.2-7.5% as senior citizen deposits are 27-30% of total deposits.

Competition on yields has intensified from private and public sector banks; management said concession pricing has moved ahead and it may have to cut rates to existing and new borrowers to retain accounts.
Corporate lending: management chose to lean into BBB-rated accounts with gating conditions, with the stated aim of lifting RWA density, while acknowledging fierce competition for AAA/AA names.
Gold loans: jewel loans are 30% of the book against an internal cap of 35%; agri gold yields are about 10.75-11%, and management plans to cut pricing toward 9.5-9% to limit growth.
Working capital utilisation fell 2-3% across sectors in Q4, as customers ran down lines amid geopolitical uncertainty; textile is flagged as the most exposed sector.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 NIM guidance versus the FY26 beat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 3.75-3.8% for FY27, citing sticky deposit costs, leakage of existing customers to competitors, and the need to concede yields to retain top line, accepting some NIM compromise.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the competitive pressure on yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said concession pricing has moved and the bank has held rates, but it now must cut to retain good accounts. Retaining accounts is a priority over margins; Q4 yield benefit of 16 bps came from repricing of 25-30% of the book.

qa_highlights.question: What sectors received the INR163 crore prudential provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Textiles, ceramics, fertilisers, chemicals, granite and quartz, plus other sectors with direct or indirect geopolitical exposure; provisioning was set on a portfolio basis after sector reviews.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ECL transition and steady-state credit cost be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still reviewing the final RBI ECL guidelines and will share clarity later; FY27 credit cost is guided below 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 credit growth guided lower than FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank chose a prudent, moderated approach in a benign-but-volatile environment to avoid credit cost offsetting yield gains, with capital not the binding constraint.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold loan LTV and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gold loans are capped at 75% LTV for retail and 80-85% for agri, with margin of 20-40%; loans above 75% LTV are under 1-1.5% of the portfolio.

risks_watch: NIM trajectory: FY27 guided at 3.75-3.8% vs 3.97% in FY26, with the retail deposit repricing impact to be seen in Q1 FY27.
Yield pressure from competition and existing-customer leakage in corporate, MSME and LAP segments.
Geopolitical exposure: INR163 crore prudential buffer on textiles, ceramics, chemicals and others; West Asia conflict impact on input costs and working capital demand.
Gold price risk: jewel loans at 30% of book; management says a 40% gold price fall would not breach LTV buffers.
ECL transition impact on steady-state credit cost is not yet quantified.
Wage revision provision from November 2026 (IBA committee not yet formed) is not yet provided.
Deposit franchise: term deposit renewals of 70-75% in retail; the flow of new deposits may be insufficient, which may push up cost of funds.

590003|2026-06.headline: KVB Q1 FY27 net profit rose 45% YoY to INR756 crore, but NIM of 4.26% and sequentially lower write-off recoveries (INR103 crore vs INR216 crore) weigh on the outlook.
590003|2026-06.overview: Karur Vysya Bank reported Q1 FY27 net profit of INR756 crore, up 4% QoQ and 45% YoY, with NIM of 4.26% and ROA of 2.11%. Total business grew 16% YoY to INR2,27,267 crore, with advances and deposits each up 6% QoQ. Sequentially, operating profit fell 12% to INR1,096 crore and non-interest income fell 28% to INR442 crore, mainly on lower write-off recoveries and one-offs. Management kept the full-year NIM guidance of 3.7% to 3.8% but said NIM should be above 4% next quarter, and it will review full-year guidance at end-September.

Fixed-rate book rose from 29% to 34% of advances; MCLR-linked book fell from 14% to 9%; EBLR-linked book stayed at 55%.
Gold loans: average blended yield is about 11% to 12%, with agri PSL benefit possibly taking it to 11.25%. Gold loans are about 30% of advances, against an internal ceiling of 30% to 35%.

Deposit pricing: time deposit rates were raised 40 bp during the quarter to fund front-loaded advances. FCNR(B) pricing is at about 7%, targeting tickets below USD1 million; base is about USD130 million.
Textiles are about 5% of the portfolio and seen as the main war-related risk. Working capital utilisation is steady at 77% to 80%. Management said the bank has not seen SMA build-up as a result.

qa_highlights.question: Will credit growth stay 100-200 bp above system if system growth has moved to around 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stay about 1% above RAM system growth, but will be more cautious in corporate to avoid repeating the earlier mistake. Corporate is now 14% of advances, down from 45%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SME YoY growth slow to 12-13%?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY26 was flat because the bank avoided pricing competition and some weak accounts. Q1 growth recovered to 6% QoQ, with commercial disbursements up 45% YoY on NTB plus ETB. Management expects about 18% growth for the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECLGS disbursement and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: In commercial, 2,232 applications were received on JanSamarth. INR140 crore disbursed, with INR10 crore in Q1. In corporate, 54 applied and INR80 crore disbursed, with 176 units eligible, of which about 100 may qualify.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold loan blended yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a blended 11% to 12%, with agri PSL benefits possibly pushing it to 11.25%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the bank pushing a higher fixed-rate book if costs are rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fixed-rate loans at 11% to 15% insulate yields if rates fall later, and 20 to 30 bp of cost increase is manageable.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about full-year NIM given the Q2 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 NIM should be 4%+ but full-year guidance of 3.7% to 3.8% is not changed and will be reviewed at end-September. Downside is limited, though a fall to 3.6% to 3.5% would be a concern.

qa_highlights.question: How will the normalisation of write-off recoveries affect ROA over the next 2 to 3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lower write-offs could cut ROA by about 25 bp, not 40-45 bp. Offsets: non-fund income (TPP and guarantees), and 10-15 bp from CASA cost and 10 bp from other income.

risks_watch: Write-off recoveries are lumpy and fell to INR103 crore; full-year target of INR500 to 600 crore is at risk if recoveries stay subdued.

SMA-30 rose from 0.17% to 0.22%; slippage ratio is guided below 1%. Textile (about 5% of book), ceramics, logistics and the El Nino/monsoon delay are the main sector watch items.

590003|2026-09.headline: KVB Q2 FY27: net profit INR788 crores (+37% YoY), NIM held at 4.26%, credit cost 0.43%, and advances growth guided to 18-20% for FY27.
590003|2026-09.overview: Karur Vysya Bank reported a strong Q2 FY27 with net profit of INR788 crores, up 4% QoQ and 37% YoY, and operating profit of INR1,162 crores (+14% YoY, +6% QoQ). Total business reached INR2,39,712 crores (+5% QoQ, +18% YoY), with advances up 7% QoQ to INR1,11,589 crores and deposits up 5% QoQ to INR1,28,123 crores. Management guided to 18-20% credit growth, NIM of 4% plus, ROA of about 2% and GNPA below 1.5% for FY27, while flagging that funding costs and loan-yield competition may pressure margins in coming quarters. Management also said the write-off recovery contribution has fallen sharply, and that the bank will rely more on core earnings.

financial_highlights.change: +INR1 crore QoQ; AS-15 provisions lower by INR28 crores

financial_highlights.value: 0.43% annualised (INR94 crores NPA/standard/restructured + INR25 crores floating provision)

segments.name: Retail advances
segments.commentary: Grew 5% QoQ led by mortgages (+12% QoQ) and personal loans (+11% QoQ); retail jewel loans fell 1% to a total jewel book of INR32,153 crores (29% of advances), with LTV of 67% for agri gold and 59% for non-agri gold.

segments.name: Corporate and institutional
segments.commentary: Portfolio grew 12% QoQ (14% of advances), with average ticket size of INR42 crores; credit substitutes grew about INR500 crores in the quarter.

segments.name: Commercial business (SBG and BBG)
segments.commentary: Grew 8% QoQ, with disbursements up about 24% QoQ; tailor-made products (GST surrogate, open term loan) crossed INR450 crores outstanding.
